Symbologies Reference

Point of Sale

EAN-13

EAN-13 is an extension of the UPC-A barcode symbology that usually carries a GTIN-13.

An EAN-13 whose first digit is 0 has the same bars as the UPC-A carrying the remaining twelve digits: EAN-13 encodes its leading digit by mirroring some of the symbol characters in the left half, and for a leading 0 none are mirrored.

Also known as: EAN, European Article Number, International Article Number, JAN, JAN-13, IAN, WPC, SAAN, UCCET, ABAC, BCCI, ICA, MANA, KANC, ANA, ANC.

Misnomers: UCC-13, GTIN-13.

Uses:

  • Retail products scanned at point of sale.
  • In-store items, such as weighed goods with price-embedded labels from a scale, using restricted circulation numbers (beginning 02, 04 or 20 to 29).
  • Store, national and euro coupons (beginning 99, or 981 to 983).

Variants:

  • EAN-13+2 is an extension of EAN-13 that includes a two-digit add-on.
  • EAN-13+5 is an extension of EAN-13 that includes a five-digit add-on.
  • EAN-99 is a special form of EAN-13 starting with 99 that is used as an in-store coupon.
  • EAN-8 is a barcode symbology derived from EAN-13 that is designed for small packaging. It uses a distinct numbering system based on GTIN-8.
  • ISBN is a variant of EAN-13 used to identify books.
  • ISMN is a variant of EAN-13 used to identify printed music.
  • ISSN is a variant of EAN-13 used to identify periodicals.
  • EAN-13 Composite is a variant of EAN-13 that should be used when a CC-A or CC-B GS1 Composite 2D component is required.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15420, BS EN 797, GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data field for an EAN-13 may contain twelve or thirteen digits, optionally followed by a space then two or five digits if an EAN-2 or EAN-5 add-on is required.
  • If twelve digits of primary data are supplied then the check digit is calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided check digit will be verified.
  • The includetext option should normally be supplied.
  • The guardwhitespace option enables the display of whitespace guard marks.
  • The guarddescent option controls how far the guard bars extend below the data bars, in multiples of the X-dimension (default: 5).
  • The addondescent option controls how far the add-on bars extend below the baseline, in multiples of the X-dimension (defaults to the value of guarddescent).

Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

Data:    9520123456788
Options: includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: ean13
Data:    952012345678
Options: includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: ean13

A symbol that includes a five-digit add-on:

Data:    952012345678 54499
Options: includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: ean13

EAN-8

EAN-8 is derived from the EAN-13 barcode symbology and is designed for small packaging. It usually carries a GTIN-8.

A GTIN-8 is assigned individually, on request, by a GS1 Member Organisation for an item whose packaging is too small for an EAN-13.

Also known as: JAN-8.

Misnomers: UCC-8.

Uses:

  • Retail products whose packaging is too small for an EAN-13.
  • In-store items using restricted circulation numbers (beginning 0 or 2).

Variants:

  • EAN-Velocity is a special form of EAN-8 starting with 0 that is used for numbering items within a company.
  • EAN-13 is a longer variant of EAN-8 which has a distinct number system based on GTIN-13.
  • EAN-8 Composite is a variant of EAN-8 that should be used when a CC-A or CC-B GS1 composite 2D component is required.
  • EAN-8+2 is a non-standard extension of EAN-8 that includes a two-digit add-on.
  • EAN-8+5 is a non-standard extension of EAN-8 that includes a five-digit add-on.
  • Marks & Spencer is a derivative of EAN-8 used by the UK retailer.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15420, BS EN 797, GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data field takes either seven or eight digits.
  • When the permitaddon option is provided, the initial seven or eight digits can be followed by a space then two or five digits where a EAN-2 or EAN-5 add-on is required (non-standard).
  • If seven digits of primary data are supplied then the check digit is calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided check digit will be verified.
  • The includetext option should normally be supplied.
  • The guardwhitespace option enables the display of whitespace guard marks.
  • The guarddescent option controls how far the guard bars extend below the data bars, in multiples of the X-dimension (default: 5).
  • The addondescent option controls how far the add-on bars extend below the baseline, in multiples of the X-dimension (defaults to the value of guarddescent).

Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

Data:    95200002
Options: includetext
Encoder: ean8
Data:    9520000
Options: includetext
Encoder: ean8

Truncated with whitespace guards:

Data:    95200002
Options: includetext height=0.5 guardwhitespace
Encoder: ean8

UPC-A

The UPC-A barcode symbology is used for identification of retail goods at point of sale. It usually carries a GTIN-12.

A UPC-A has the same bars as an EAN-13 whose first digit is 0. EAN-13 encodes its additional leading digit by mirroring some of the symbol characters in the left half, and for a leading 0 none are mirrored.

Also known as: UPC, Universal Product Code.

Misnomers: UCC-12.

Uses:

  • Retail products scanned at point of sale, chiefly in the US and Canada.
  • In-store items, such as weighed goods with price-embedded labels from a scale, using restricted circulation numbers (beginning 2 or 4).

Variants:

  • UPC-A+2 is an extension of UPC-A that includes a two-digit add-on.
  • UPC-A+5 is an extension of UPC-A that includes a five-digit add-on.
  • UPC-E is a barcode symbology derived from UPC-A that is designed for small packaging.
  • UPC-A Composite is a variant of UPC-A that should be used when a CC-A or CC-B GS1 composite 2D component is required.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15420, BS EN 797, GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data field for a UPC-A may contain eleven or twelve digits, optionally followed by a space then two or five digits if an EAN-2 or EAN-5 add-on is required.
  • Alternatively, the data field may contain seven or eight digits of a UPC-E to produce the equivalent UPC-A symbol.
  • If eleven digits of primary data are supplied then the check digit is calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided check digit will be verified.
  • The includetext option should normally be supplied.
  • The guardwhitespace option enables the display of whitespace guard marks.
  • The guarddescent option controls how far the guard bars extend below the data bars, in multiples of the X-dimension (default: 5).
  • The addondescent option controls how far the add-on bars extend below the baseline, in multiples of the X-dimension (defaults to the value of guarddescent).

Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

Data:    012345000058
Options: includetext
Encoder: upca
Data:    01234500005
Options: includetext
Encoder: upca

A symbol that includes a five-digit add-on:

Data:    012345000058 54499
Options: includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: upca

UPC-E

UPC-E is a compacted form of the UPC-A barcode symbology that usually carries a GTIN-12 that has been zero compressed.

Also known as: UPC-E0.

Uses:

  • Retail products whose packaging is too small for a UPC-A.

Variants:

  • UPC-E+2 is an extension of UPC-E that includes a two-digit add-on.
  • UPC-E+5 is an extension of UPC-E that includes a five-digit add-on.
  • UPC-A is the full size form of UPC-E.
  • UPC-E Composite is a variant of UPC-E that should be used when a CC-A or CC-B GS1 Composite 2D component is required.
  • UPC-E1 is a UPC-E with a number system of 1. This is not defined by any symbology standard.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15420, BS EN 797, GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data field takes either seven or eight digits, optionally followed by a space then two or five digits if an EAN-2 or EAN-5 add-on is required.
  • Alternatively, the data field may contain eleven or twelve digits of a UPC-A to produce the equivalent UPC-E symbol, provided that the input can be zero suppressed.
  • If seven digits of primary data are supplied then the check digit is calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided check digit will be verified.
  • The primary data must start with "0", or "1" for a UPC-E1.
  • The includetext option should normally be supplied.
  • The guarddescent option controls how far the guard bars extend below the data bars, in multiples of the X-dimension (default: 5).
  • The addondescent option controls how far the add-on bars extend below the baseline, in multiples of the X-dimension (defaults to the value of guarddescent).

Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

Data:    01234558
Options: includetext
Encoder: upce
Data:    0123455
Options: includetext
Encoder: upce

A truncated symbol:

Data:    01234558
Options: includetext height=0.5
Encoder: upce

ISBN

An ISBN barcode is a variant of EAN-13 that is used to identify books.

Also known as: ISBN-13, International Standard Book Number, Bookland EAN, Bookland EAN-13.

Uses:

  • Books.

Variants:

  • ISBN-10 is a legacy format that was deprecated for public use after 1st January 2007.

Standards: ISO 2108, ISO/IEC 15420, BS EN 797, GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data should contain twelve or thirteen digits separated appropriately by dash characters -.
  • The data can also be provided in legacy ISBN-10 format as nine or ten digits separated appropriately by dash characters -. This will be automatically upgraded to the ISBN-13 format.
  • If the last digit of the primary data is not given then the ISBN check digit is calculated automatically, otherwise it will be verified.
  • The primary data can optionally be followed by a space then five digits if an EAN-5 add-on is required, typically to encode the book's price (see Price Add-On below).
  • The includetext option should normally be supplied.
  • The guardwhitespace option enables the display of whitespace guard marks.
  • The following options control the placement and styling of the ISBN text above the symbol. Each is equivalent to the corresponding extratext* option:
    • isbntext: Override the ISBN label content
    • isbntextfont: PostScript font name for text above symbol
    • isbntextsize: Font size for the text above symbol, in points
    • isbntextcolor: Colour for the text above symbol
    • isbntextxalign, isbntextyalign: Alignment of the text above symbol
    • isbntextxoffset, isbntextyoffset: Position of the text above symbol, in points
    • isbntextdirection: Direction of the text above symbol
    • isbntextgaps: Gap between characters in the text above symbol, in points
    • isbntextsubspace, isbntextsplit, isbntextlinegaps: See Text Properties
  • Deprecated. The legacy option shows the ISBN-10 above the symbol in place of the ISBN-13. The bars are the same.

Price Add-On

A five-digit add-on encodes the book's price as a currency digit followed by four digits of price, under conventions set by each market's book industry. The International ISBN Agency's users' manual says the add-on carries a price only in the United States and Canada, and that elsewhere it may be used for a publisher's in-house purposes. Check the local convention with the ISBN agency or trading partners.

Add-on Conventional Meaning
00001 to 09999 Price in pounds sterling, £0.01 to £99.99
10000 to 49999 Price in US dollars, US$100.00 to US$499.99
50001 to 59998 Price in US dollars, US$0.01 to US$99.98
59999 Formerly, a price in US dollars above US$99.98 (US$99.99 cannot be encoded)
60001 to 69999 Price in Canadian dollars, CA$0.01 to CA$99.99
90000 to 98999 For the publisher's own in-house use, such as handling returns
99990 A used book (US college stores)
99991 A desk copy (US college stores)
  • In the UK, booksellers look up a book's price from its ISBN, so the symbol without an add-on is generally recommended. UK publishers selling into the US add the US price.
  • In Korea, the add-on carries the Korean book number's additional code rather than a price: a readership digit, a publication form digit and a three-digit subject classification from the Korean Decimal Classification.
  • Sources: International ISBN Agency, ISBN Users' Manual; Book Industry Study Group, Barcoding Guidelines for the US Book Industry; Book Industry Communication, Bar Coding for Books; BookNet Canada, Product Bar Codes; National Library of Korea, Korean ISBN and ISSN Manual.

Examples

ISBN-13

Identical symbols, input provided with and without an ISBN check digit:

Data:    978-1-873671-00-9
Options: includetext
Encoder: isbn
Data:    978-1-873671-00
Options: includetext
Encoder: isbn

An ISBN with a five-digit add-on:

Data:    978-1-873671-00-9 54499
Options: includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: isbn

The following ISBN-10 input will be automatically upgraded to a valid ISBN-13 symbol:

Data:    1-86074-271-8
Options: includetext
Encoder: isbn
Data:    1-86074-271
Options: includetext
Encoder: isbn

ISBN-10 label (Legacy)

The following show the ISBN-10 above the symbol:

Data:    1-86074-271-8
Options: legacy includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: isbn
Data:    1-86074-271
Options: legacy includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: isbn

Styling the ISBN label

The ISBN label can be styled using the isbntext* options (or the equivalent extratext*):

Data:    978-1-873671-00-9
Options: includetext isbntextcolor=FF0000 isbntextxalign=center
Encoder: isbn

ISMN

An ISMN barcode is a variant of EAN-13 with a prefix 979 that is used to identify printed music.

Also known as: International Standard Music Number, ISMN-13, Musicland EAN-13.

Uses:

  • Printed music.

Variants:

  • ISMN-10 is a legacy format that was deprecated for public use.

Standards: ISO 10957, ISO/IEC 15420, BS EN 797, GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data should contain twelve or thirteen digits separated appropriately by dash characters -.
  • The data can also be provided in legacy ISMN-10 format start M- then eight or nine digits separated appropriately by dash characters -. This will be automatically upgraded to the ISMN-13 format.
  • If the last digit of the primary data is not given then the ISMN check digit is calculated automatically, otherwise it will be verified.
  • The primary data can optionally be followed by a space and two or five digits for an EAN-2 or EAN-5 add-on.
  • The includetext option should normally be supplied.
  • The guardwhitespace option enables the display of whitespace guard marks.
  • The following options control the placement and styling of the ISMN text above the symbol. Each is equivalent to the corresponding extratext* option:
    • ismntext: Override the ISMN label content
    • ismntextfont: PostScript font name for text above symbol
    • ismntextsize: Font size for the text above symbol, in points
    • ismntextcolor: Colour for the text above symbol
    • ismntextxalign, ismntextyalign: Alignment of the text above symbol
    • ismntextxoffset, ismntextyoffset: Position of the text above symbol, in points
    • ismntextdirection: Direction of the text above symbol
    • ismntextgaps: Gap between characters in the text above symbol, in points
    • ismntextsubspace, ismntextsplit, ismntextlinegaps: See Text Properties
  • Deprecated. The legacy option shows the ISMN-10 above the symbol in place of the ISMN-13. The bars are the same.

Examples

ISMN-13

Identical symbols, input provided with and without an ISMN check digit:

Data:    979-0-2600-0043-8
Options: includetext
Encoder: ismn
Data:    979-0-2600-0043
Options: includetext
Encoder: ismn

The following ISMN-10 input will be automatically upgraded to a valid ISMN-13 symbol:

Data:    M-345-24680-5
Options: includetext
Encoder: ismn
Data:    M-345-24680
Options: includetext
Encoder: ismn

ISMN-10 label (Legacy)

The following show the ISMN-10 above the symbol:

Data:    M-345-24680-5
Options: legacy includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: ismn
Data:    M-345-24680
Options: legacy includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: ismn

Styling the ISMN label

The ISMN label can be styled using the ismntext* options (or the equivalent extratext*):

Data:    979-0-2600-0043-8
Options: includetext ismntextcolor=FF0000 ismntextxalign=center
Encoder: ismn

ISSN

An ISSN barcode is an EAN-13 with prefix 977 used to identify periodicals.

Also known as: International Standard Serial Number.

Uses:

  • Magazines, newspapers and other periodicals, with the issue number in an add-on.

Standards: ISO 3297, ISO/IEC 15420, BS EN 797, GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data should contain the seven or eight digits ISSN separated by a dash character -, optionally followed by a two-digit sequence variant (00 when not given; it usually starts at zero and is incremented whenever the recommended retail price is amended), and then optionally by two or five digits if a two-digit add-on or five-digit add-on is required.
    • The add-on usually indicates the issue number, according to the ISSN International Centre.
    • In the UK, the PPA's barcoding guidelines specify a two-digit add-on identifying each issue.
    • A five-digit add-on can be used instead of a two-digit one where the publisher's numbering needs it, such as the actual date of issue, according to the GS1 General Specifications. The two cannot be used together.
  • If the last digit of the ISSN data is not given then the ISSN check digit is calculated automatically, otherwise it will be verified.
  • The includetext option should normally be supplied.
  • The guardwhitespace option enables the display of whitespace guard marks.
  • The following options control the placement and styling of the ISSN text above the symbol. Each is equivalent to the corresponding extratext* option:
    • issntext: Override the ISSN label content
    • issntextfont: PostScript font name for text above symbol
    • issntextsize: Font size for the text above symbol, in points
    • issntextcolor: Colour for the text above symbol
    • issntextxalign, issntextyalign: Alignment of the text above symbol
    • issntextxoffset, issntextyoffset: Position of the text above symbol, in points
    • issntextdirection: Direction of the text above symbol
    • issntextgaps: Gap between characters in the text above symbol, in points
    • issntextsubspace, issntextsplit, issntextlinegaps: See Text Properties

Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without an ISSN check digit and having sequence variant 00:

Data:    0317-8471 00
Options: includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: issn
Data:    0317-847 00
Options: includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: issn

An ISSN with sequence variant 03 and a two-digit add-on representing issue number 17:

Data:    0317-8471 03 17
Options: includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: issn
Data:    0317-847 03 17
Options: includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: issn

The ISSN label can be styled using the issntext* options (or the equivalent extratext*):

Data:    0317-8471 00
Options: includetext guardwhitespace issntextcolor=FF0000 issntextxalign=center
Encoder: issn

Two-Dimensional

Aztec Code

Aztec Code is a 2D matrix-style barcode symbology. It can encode full 256-character extended-ASCII.

Uses:

  • Mobile airline boarding passes (IATA Bar Coded Boarding Pass).
  • European rail tickets (UIC Flexible Content Barcode).

Variants:

  • Compact Aztec Code is a reduced form of Aztec Code used in applications where the space for the symbol is restricted.
  • Aztec Runes are a set of small barcode symbols that are used for special applications.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24778, ANSI/AIM BC13 - ISS Aztec Code.

Data and Options

  • The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1. When supported by the receiver, characters from other code pages can be encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • When the parsefnc option is specified, non-data function characters can be specified by escape sequences:
    • ^FNC1: FNC1
    • ^ECI000000 to ^ECI999999: ECI indicators
    • ^FNC@: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g. ^FNC@T... or ^FNC@99.... See FNC1 in second position.
    • ECIs are not available with FNC1 in first or second position.
  • The eclevel option is used to specify the percentage of error correction to be applied when expanding the data, from 5 to 95, by default 23.
  • The ecaddchars option is used to specify how many additional error correction characters to add after applying the eclevel percentage, 3 or more, by default 3.
  • The layers option is used to specify a particular number of layers in which to encode the data, between 1 and 32. By default the encoder will create a symbol with the minimal number of layers to encode the given data.
  • The readerinit option denotes that the symbol is used for programming the barcode reader. Reader programming is only compatible with 1- to 22-layer full-range Aztec Code symbols, so layers must also be given, from 1 to 22.
  • The raw option denotes that the data field is providing the input as a pre-encoded bitstream suitable for direct low-level encoding.
  • Deprecated: Consider Compact Aztec Code instead. The format option can also be used to create Compact Aztec Code symbols, using format=compact.
  • Deprecated: Consider Aztec Runes instead. The format option can also be used to create Aztec Code "runes", using format=rune. In this case the rune symbol number should be given in the data field.
  • The sampos, samtotal and samid options make the symbol one of a Structured Append sequence of 2 to 26 symbols, which a reader reassembles into a single message. sampos and samtotal are required:
    • sampos is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to samtotal.
    • samtotal is the number of symbols in the sequence.
    • samid is an optional message ID, which is the same in every symbol of the sequence and must not contain spaces. Uppercase letters encode most compactly.
    • Structured Append is not available for Aztec Runes, reader initialisation symbols or with the raw option.

Examples

A symbol with a fixed number of layers:

Data:    ABC123
Options: layers=3
Encoder: azteccode

A symbol with additional error correction characters:

Data:    TEST
Options: ecaddchars=20 layers=4
Encoder: azteccode

Compact Aztec Code

Compact Aztec Code is a reduced form of the Aztec Code barcode that is used in applications where the space for the symbol is restricted.

Variants:

  • Aztec Code is the larger, more popular variant.
  • Aztec Runes are a set of small barcode symbols that are used for special applications.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24778, ANSI/AIM BC13 - ISS Aztec Code.

Data and Options

  • The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1. When supported by the receiver, characters from other code pages can be encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • When the parsefnc option is specified, non-data function characters can be specified by escape sequences:
    • ^FNC1: FNC1
    • ^ECI000000 to ^ECI999999: ECI indicators
    • ^FNC@: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g. ^FNC@T... or ^FNC@99.... See FNC1 in second position.
    • ECIs are not available with FNC1 in first or second position.
  • The eclevel option is used to specify the percentage of error correction to be applied when expanding the data, from 5 to 95, by default 23.
  • The ecaddchars option is used to specify how many additional error correction characters to add after applying the eclevel percentage, 3 or more, by default 3.
  • The layers option is used to specify a particular number of layers in which to encode the data, between 1 and 4. By default the encoder will create a symbol with the minimal number of layers to encode the given data.
  • The readerinit option denotes that the symbol is used for programming the barcode reader. Reader programming is only compatible with 1-layer Compact Aztec Code symbols.
  • The raw option denotes that the data field is providing the input as a pre-encoded bitstream suitable for direct low-level encoding.
  • The sampos, samtotal and samid options make the symbol one of a Structured Append sequence of 2 to 26 symbols, which a reader reassembles into a single message. sampos and samtotal are required:
    • sampos is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to samtotal.
    • samtotal is the number of symbols in the sequence.
    • samid is an optional message ID, which is the same in every symbol of the sequence and must not contain spaces. Uppercase letters encode most compactly.
    • Structured Append is not available for reader initialisation symbols or with the raw option.

Examples

A basic symbol:

Data:    This is Compact Aztec Code
Options:
Encoder: azteccodecompact

A symbol using the parse option with increased error correction:

Data:    This is ^065ztec Code
Options: parse eclevel=50 ecaddchars=5
Encoder: azteccodecompact

A minimal symbol:

Data:    ABC123
Options:
Encoder: azteccodecompact

A symbol using raw bitstream input:

Data:    00100111001000000101001101111000010100111100101000000110
Options: raw
Encoder: azteccodecompact

Aztec Runes

Aztec Runes are a set of small Aztec Code symbols that are used for special applications.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24778, ANSI/AIM BC13 - ISS Aztec Code.

Data and Options

  • The data field contains the rune number 0 to 255.

Examples

A rune encoding the value 25:

Data:    25
Options:
Encoder: aztecrune

Data Matrix

The Data Matrix symbology is a 2D matrix-style barcode that can encode full 256 character extended-ASCII.

Also known as: Data Matrix ECC 200, DataMatrix.

Uses:

  • Marking small parts and electronic components, and direct part marking.
  • Mobile airline boarding passes (IATA Bar Coded Boarding Pass).
  • Unit packets and aggregated packaging of tobacco products under EU traceability Regulation (EU) 2018/574.
  • US military part marking under the Department of Defense IUID rules (MIL-STD-130), carrying an ISO/IEC 15434 message.
  • German pharmacy packs under securPharm in the IFA format, carrying the PPN in an ISO/IEC 15434 message.
  • Electronic component reel and bag labels (ECIA EIGP 114).
  • Postage printed by franking machines, online and on stamps, such as Deutsche Post's Matrixcode.
  • Blood, tissue and cell products labelled to ISBT 128.
  • Automotive transport labels (Global Transport Label: Odette, AIAG B-16, VDA 4994).
  • Aircraft parts, marked to ATA Spec 2000 Chapter 9 (SAE AS9132).
  • Back-surface marking of silicon wafers (SEMI T7).

Variants:

  • Data Matrix Rectangular is a variant of Data Matrix that uses rectangular symbols.
  • Data Matrix Rectangular Extension is a variant of Data Matrix Rectangular that provides a greater range of symbol dimensions.
  • GS1 DataMatrix is a variant of Data Matrix that should be used when encoding data that is in GS1 Application Identifier standard format.
  • GS1 Digital Link Data Matrix is a variant of Data Matrix that should be used when encoding a GS1 Digital Link URI.
  • HIBC Data Matrix is a variant of Data Matrix that should be used when encoding HIBC formatted data.
  • Royal Mail Mailmark is a variant of Data Matrix that is used by the Royal Mail postal service on letters and other small mailpieces.
  • PPN-Code is a variant of Data Matrix that carries the Pharmacy Product Number and pack data of pharmaceutical packs.

Standards: ISO/IEC 16022, ANSI/AIM BC11 - ISS Data Matrix.

Data and Options

  • The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1. When supported by the receiver, characters from other code pages can be encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value. This is useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • When the parsefnc option is specified, non-data function characters can be specified by escape sequences:
    • ^FNC1: FNC1. Recommendation: Consider GS1 DataMatrix for encoding GS1 AI syntax data.
    • ^PROG: PROG - Reader programming
    • ^ECI000000 to ^ECI999999: ECI indicators
    • ^FNC@: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g. ^FNC@T... or ^FNC@99.... See FNC1 in second position.
    • ECIs are not available with FNC1 in first or second position.
  • The encoder compresses ISO/IEC 15434 messages in Format 05 or 06, except in a Structured Append symbol.
  • The sampos, samtotal and samid options make the symbol one of a Structured Append sequence of 2 to 16 symbols, which a reader reassembles into a single message. All three are required:
    • sampos is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to samtotal.
    • samtotal is the number of symbols in the sequence.
    • samid is the file identification, from 1 to 64516, and is the same in every symbol of the sequence. It distinguishes the symbols of one message from those of another.
    • An FNC1 at the start of the first symbol selects GS1 mode for the whole message. At the start of a later symbol it is a field separator.
    • FNC1 in second position is only available in the first symbol.
    • Structured Append is not available with the raw option or reader programming, nor for GS1 DataMatrix, GS1 Digital Link Data Matrix, Royal Mail Mailmark or PPN-Code symbols.
  • When the dotty option is specified the modules are rendered as dots rather than squares. The dot radius can be adjusted using the inkspread option.
  • The columns and rows options are used to specify the size of the symbol.
  • The version option can also be used to specify the symbol size, as version=RxC. Valid options are 10x10, 12x12, 14x14, 16x16, 18x18, 20x20, 22x22, 24x24, 26x26, 32x32, 36x36, 40x40, 44x44, 48x48, 52x52, 64x64, 72x72, 80x80, 88x88, 96x96, 104x104, 120x120, 132x132, 144x144
  • If columns, rows and version are unspecified the encoder will default to creating the smallest symbol that holds the data.
  • The c40headerlength option specifies the number of leading characters in the data field that must be stored using C40 encodation.
  • The raw option denotes that the data field is providing the input as pre-encoded codewords in ^NNN format, suitable for direct low-level encoding.
  • Deprecated: The format option is used to specify the shape of the symbol, either:
    • square (default)
    • rectangle: Consider Data Matrix Rectangular for rectangular symbols.
  • Deprecated: Consider Data Matrix Rectangular Extension. The dmre option enables Data Matrix Rectangular Extension symbols based on the ISO/IEC standard, which increases the number of rectangular symbol sizes available.

Examples

Identical symbols, automatically sized, the latter showing use of the parse option:

Data:    This is Data Matrix
Options: 
Encoder: datamatrix
Data:    This is ^068ata Matrix
Options: parse
Encoder: datamatrix

Identical symbols with a fixed size:

Data:    Fixed size
Options: version=48x48
Encoder: datamatrix
Data:    Fixed size
Options: rows=48 columns=48
Encoder: datamatrix

An advanced use containing "hidden data" in the padding codewords as used by some non-standard, "high-security" applications. The technique works by filling the symbol using raw codewords formed from the standard data immediately followed by the non-standard padding data beginning with ^129:

Data:    ^066^067^068^142^052^129^161^056^206^101^251^147
Options: version=16x16 raw
Encoder: datamatrix

Data Matrix Rectangular

The Data Matrix Rectangular symbology is a rectangular variant of Data Matrix.

Uses:

  • Marking narrow areas, such as the edge of a part or a narrow label.

Variants:

  • Data Matrix is the standard square variant of the symbology.
  • Data Matrix Rectangular Extension is a variant of Data Matrix Rectangular that provides a greater range of symbol dimensions.

Standards: ISO/IEC 16022, ANSI/AIM BC11 - ISS Data Matrix.

Data and Options

  • The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1. When supported by the receiver, characters from other code pages can be encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value. This is useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • When the parsefnc option is specified, non-data function characters can be specified by escape sequences:
    • ^FNC1: FNC1. Recommendation: Consider GS1 DataMatrix for encoding GS1 AI syntax data.
    • ^PROG: PROG - Reader programming
    • ^ECI000000 to ^ECI999999: ECI indicators
    • ^FNC@: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g. ^FNC@T... or ^FNC@99.... See FNC1 in second position.
    • ECIs are not available with FNC1 in first or second position.
  • The encoder compresses ISO/IEC 15434 messages in Format 05 or 06, except in a Structured Append symbol.
  • The sampos, samtotal and samid options make the symbol one of a Structured Append sequence of 2 to 16 symbols, which a reader reassembles into a single message. All three are required:
    • sampos is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to samtotal.
    • samtotal is the number of symbols in the sequence.
    • samid is the file identification, from 1 to 64516, and is the same in every symbol of the sequence. It distinguishes the symbols of one message from those of another.
    • An FNC1 at the start of the first symbol selects GS1 mode for the whole message. At the start of a later symbol it is a field separator.
    • FNC1 in second position is only available in the first symbol.
    • Structured Append is not available with the raw option or reader programming, nor for GS1 DataMatrix, GS1 Digital Link Data Matrix or Royal Mail Mailmark symbols.
  • When the dotty option is specified the modules are rendered as dots rather than squares. The dot radius can be adjusted using the inkspread option.
  • The columns and rows options are used to specify the size of the symbol.
  • The version option can also be used to specify the symbol size, as version=RxC. Valid options are 8x18, 8x32, 12x26, 12x36, 16x36, 16x48.
  • If columns, rows and version are unspecified the encoder will default to creating a symbol that is the minimum size to represent the given data.
  • The c40headerlength option specifies the number of leading characters in the data field that must be stored using C40 encodation.
  • The raw option denotes that the data field is providing the input as pre-encoded codewords in ^NNN format, suitable for direct low-level encoding.
  • Deprecated: Consider Data Matrix Rectangular Extension. The dmre option enables Data Matrix Rectangular Extension symbols based on the ISO/IEC standard, which increases the number of rectangular symbol sizes available.

Examples

A rectangular symbol with a fixed size:

Data:    Rectangular
Options: version=16x48
Encoder: datamatrixrectangular

Data Matrix Rectangular Extension

The Data Matrix Rectangular Extension symbology is an enhancement to Data Matrix Rectangular that provides a greater range of symbol dimensions.

Also known as: DMRE.

Uses:

  • Marking narrow areas with more data than a rectangular Data Matrix holds, where the readers support DMRE (ISO/IEC 21471).

Variants:

  • Data Matrix is the standard square variant of the symbology.
  • Data Matrix Rectangular is the original rectangular variant of Data Matrix that provides a limited range of symbol dimensions.

Standards: ISO/IEC 21471.

Data and Options

  • The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1. When supported by the receiver, characters from other code pages can be encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value. This is useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • When the parsefnc option is specified, non-data function characters can be specified by escape sequences:
    • ^FNC1: FNC1. Recommendation: Consider GS1 DataMatrix for encoding GS1 AI syntax data.
    • ^PROG: PROG - Reader programming
    • ^ECI000000 to ^ECI999999: ECI indicators
    • ^FNC@: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g. ^FNC@T... or ^FNC@99.... See FNC1 in second position.
    • ECIs are not available with FNC1 in first or second position.
  • The encoder compresses ISO/IEC 15434 messages in Format 05 or 06, except in a Structured Append symbol.
  • The sampos, samtotal and samid options make the symbol one of a Structured Append sequence of 2 to 16 symbols, which a reader reassembles into a single message. All three are required:
    • sampos is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to samtotal.
    • samtotal is the number of symbols in the sequence.
    • samid is the file identification, from 1 to 64516, and is the same in every symbol of the sequence. It distinguishes the symbols of one message from those of another.
    • An FNC1 at the start of the first symbol selects GS1 mode for the whole message. At the start of a later symbol it is a field separator.
    • FNC1 in second position is only available in the first symbol.
    • Structured Append is not available with the raw option or reader programming, nor for GS1 DataMatrix, GS1 Digital Link Data Matrix or Royal Mail Mailmark symbols.
  • When the dotty option is specified the modules are rendered as dots rather than squares. The dot radius can be adjusted using the inkspread option.
  • The columns and rows options are used to specify the size of the symbol.
  • The version option can also be used to specify the symbol size, as version=RxC. Valid options are 8x18, 8x32, 8x48, 8x64, 8x80, 8x96, 8x120, 8x144, 12x26, 12x36, 12x64, 12x88, 16x36, 16x48, 16x64, 20x36, 20x44, 20x64, 22x48, 24x48, 24x64, 26x40, 26x48, 26x64.
  • If columns, rows and version are unspecified the encoder will default to creating a symbol that is the minimum size to represent the given data.
  • The c40headerlength option specifies the number of leading characters in the data field that must be stored using C40 encodation.
  • The raw option denotes that the data field is providing the input as pre-encoded codewords in ^NNN format, suitable for direct low-level encoding.

Examples

A DMRE symbol with a fixed size:

Data:    1234
Options: version=8x80
Encoder: datamatrixrectangularextension

Han Xin Code

The Han Xin Code symbology is a 2D matrix-style barcode symbology that can encode full 256 character extended-ASCII.

Also known as: Chinese Sensible.

Standards: GB/T 21049-2007.

Data and Options

  • The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • When the parsefnc option is specified, ^FNC1 in the first position of the data selects GS1 mode. FNC1 cannot appear elsewhere.
  • The eclevel option is used to specify the error correction level:
    • eclevel=L1 - Lowest
    • eclevel=L2 (default)
    • eclevel=L3
    • eclevel=L4 - Highest
  • The version option is used to specify the size of the symbol, 1 to 84.
  • If unspecified the encoder will select the version of the symbol that is the minimum size to represent the given data at the selected error correction level.
  • The mask option is used to specify the mask pattern, 1 to 4. If unspecified the encoder selects the best mask.

Examples

A fixed-size symbol with maximum error correction:

Data:    Han Xin Code
Options: version=10 eclevel=L4
Encoder: hanxin

MicroPDF417

The MicroPDF417 barcode symbology is 2D stacked-linear barcode based on PDF417 that can encode full 256 character extended-ASCII.

Variants:

  • PDF417 is a larger variant of the MicroPDF417 barcode.
  • HIBC MicroPDF417 is a variant of MicroPDF417 that should be used when encoding HIBC formatted data.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24728, AIM ISS - MicroPDF417.

Data and Options

  • The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1. When supported by the receiver characters from other code pages can be encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).

  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters.

  • When the parsefnc option is specified, non-data function characters can be specified by escape sequences:

    • ^ECI000000 to ^ECI811799: ECI indicators
    • ^FNC@: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g. ^FNC@T... or ^FNC@99.... See FNC1 in second position. The symbol is encoded in Code 128 emulation, which readers report as ]C2 or ]L4. It is not available with readerinit, and only in the first symbol of a Structured Append sequence.
    • ^FNC1: FNC1, a field separator after FNC1 in second position.
    • ECIs are not available with FNC1 in second position.

  • Whenever the data field contains suitable input, the encoder will compress ISO/IEC 15434 structured data (internally using the 05 Macro and 06 Macro codewords), except in a Structured Append symbol or with readerinit.

  • The columns and rows options are used to specify the size of the symbol. Valid values, as columns x rows, are:

    • 1x11, 1x14, 1x17, 1x20, 1x24, 1x28, 2x8, 2x11, 2x14, 2x17, 2x20, 2x23, 2x26, 3x6, 3x8, 3x10, 3x12, 3x15, 3x20, 3x26, 3x32, 3x38, 3x44, 4x4, 4x6, 4x8, 4x10, 4x12, 4x15, 4x20, 4x26, 4x32, 4x38, 4x44

  • The version option can also be used to specify the symbol size, as version=RxC (rows first), for example version=15x4.

  • If the columns, rows and version are unspecified the encoder will default to creating a symbol that is the minimum size to represent the given data.

  • The rowmult option is used to specify how tall each bar is, with respect to the minimum module width. The default is 2.

  • The raw option denotes that the data field is providing the input as pre-encoded codewords in ^NNN format, suitable for direct low-level encoding.

  • The sampos, samtotal and samid options make the symbol one of a Structured Append sequence of 2 to 99999 symbols, which a reader reassembles into a single message. All three are required:

    • sampos is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to samtotal.
    • samtotal is the number of symbols in the sequence. It is encoded as the segment count, and the last symbol of the sequence is marked as such.
    • samid is the file ID, which is the same in every symbol of the sequence, given as one or more groups of three digits, each from 000 to 899, for example samid=017053.
    • The optional fields that describe the file, such as its name, sender and time stamp, are not supported.
    • Structured Append is not available with the raw option or for GS1 Composite symbols.

  • The readerinit option denotes that the symbol is used for programming the barcode reader. Every symbol of a Structured Append sequence for reader programming is given it. It is not available with the raw option or for GS1 Composite symbols.

  • Deprecated: Internal use. The cca option identifies this symbol as a CC-A 2D component of a GS1 Composite symbol.

    • Special size rules apply when the cca option is given, in which case the columns and rows options that are used to specify the size of the symbol must be one of:
      • 2x5, 2x6, 2x7, 2x8, 2x9, 2x10, 2x12, 3x4, 3x5, 3x6, 3x7, 3x8, 4x3, 4x4, 4x5, 4x6, 4x7

  • Deprecated: Internal use. The ccb option identifies this symbol as a CC-B 2D component of a GS1 Composite symbol.

Examples

A basic symbol:

Data:    MicroPDF417
Options:
Encoder: micropdf417

A symbol using the parse option with fixed dimensions:

Data:    MicroP^068F417
Options: parse rows=15 columns=4
Encoder: micropdf417

PDF417

The PDF417 barcode symbology is 2D stacked-linear barcode that can encode full 256 character extended-ASCII.

Uses:

  • North American driver's licences and identity cards (AAMVA DL/ID Card Design Standard).
  • Printed airline boarding passes (IATA Bar Coded Boarding Pass).
  • Automotive transport labels (Global Transport Label: Odette, AIAG B-16, VDA 4994).

Variants:

  • Compact PDF417 is a shortened form of the PDF417 barcode that is used in applications where the space for the symbol is restricted.
  • MicroPDF417 is a smaller variant of the PDF417 barcode.
  • HIBC PDF417 is a variant of PDF417 that should be used when encoding HIBC formatted data.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15438, DD ENV 12925, AIM USS - PDF417.

Data and Options

  • The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1. When supported by the receiver characters from other code pages can be encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • When the parsefnc option is specified, non-data function characters can be specified by escape sequences:
    • ^ECI000000 to ^ECI811799: ECI indicators.
  • The eclevel option is used to specify the error correction level, from 0 to 8. The default is to choose a standard level of error correction that is determined by the encoded data length.
  • The fixedeclevel option will prevent the error correction level from being opportunistically raised when a better fit to the current matrix is possible.
  • The columns option specifies the number of columns (or groups of bars) in the output symbol, from 1 to 30.
  • The rows option specifies the minimum number of rows in the symbol, from 3 to 90.
  • If rows is unspecified the encoder will select a number that creates a symbol that is the minimum size to represent the given data.
  • The rowmult option is used to specify how tall each bar is, with respect to the minimum module width. The default is 3.
  • The raw option denotes that the data field is providing the input as pre-encoded codewords in ^NNN format, suitable for direct low-level encoding.
  • The sampos, samtotal and samid options make the symbol one of a Macro PDF417 sequence of 2 to 99999 symbols, which a reader reassembles into a single message. All three are required:
    • sampos is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to samtotal.
    • samtotal is the number of symbols in the sequence. It is encoded as the segment count, and the last symbol of the sequence is marked as such.
    • samid is the file ID, which is the same in every symbol of the sequence, given as one or more groups of three digits, each from 000 to 899, for example samid=017053.
    • The optional fields that describe the file, such as its name, sender and time stamp, are not supported.
    • Macro PDF417 is not available with the raw option or for GS1 Composite symbols.
  • The readerinit option denotes that the symbol is used for programming the barcode reader. Every symbol of a Macro PDF417 sequence for reader programming is given it. It is not available with the raw option or for GS1 Composite symbols.
  • Deprecated: Use Compact PDF417 instead. The compact option is used to create a compact/truncated PDF417 symbol that has fewer bars per row than a standard symbol and hence is more narrow.
  • Deprecated: Internal use. The ccc option identifies this symbol as a CC-C 2D component of a GS1 Composite symbol.

Examples

A basic symbol:

Data:    PDF417
Options:
Encoder: pdf417

A symbol using the parse option with fixed dimensions:

Data:    P^068F417
Options: parse columns=2 rows=15
Encoder: pdf417

A symbol with increased error correction:

Data:    Strong error correction
Options: columns=2 eclevel=5
Encoder: pdf417

A symbol using raw codeword input:

Data:    ^453^178^121^239
Options: raw columns=2
Encoder: pdf417

Compact PDF417

Compact PDF417 is a shortened form of the PDF417 barcode that is used in applications where the space for the symbol is restricted.

Also known as: Truncated PDF417.

Variants:

  • PDF417 is the larger, more popular variant.
  • MicroPDF417 is a smaller variant of the PDF417 barcode.
  • HIBC PDF417 is a variant of PDF417 that should be used when encoding HIBC formatted data.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15438, DD ENV 12925, AIM USS - PDF417.

Data and Options

  • The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1. When supported by the receiver, characters from other code pages can be encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • When the parsefnc option is specified, non-data function characters can be specified by escape sequences:
    • ^ECI000000 to ^ECI811799: ECI indicators
  • The eclevel option is used to specify the error correction level, from 0 to 8. The default is to choose a standard level of error correction that is determined by the encoded data length.
  • The fixedeclevel option will prevent the error correction level from being opportunistically raised when a better fit to the current matrix is possible.
  • The columns option specifies the number of columns (or groups of bars) in the output symbol, from 1 to 30.
  • The rows option specifies the minimum number of rows in the symbol, from 3 to 90.
  • If rows is unspecified the encoder will select a number that creates a symbol that is the minimum size to represent the given data.
  • The rowmult option is used to specify how tall each bar is, with respect to the minimum module width. The default is 3.
  • The raw option denotes that the data field is providing the input as pre-encoded codewords in ^NNN format, suitable for direct low-level encoding.
  • The sampos, samtotal and samid options make the symbol one of a Macro PDF417 sequence of 2 to 99999 symbols, which a reader reassembles into a single message. All three are required:
    • sampos is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to samtotal.
    • samtotal is the number of symbols in the sequence. It is encoded as the segment count, and the last symbol of the sequence is marked as such.
    • samid is the file ID, which is the same in every symbol of the sequence, given as one or more groups of three digits, each from 000 to 899, for example samid=017053.
    • The optional fields that describe the file, such as its name, sender and time stamp, are not supported.
    • Macro PDF417 is not available with the raw option.
  • The readerinit option denotes that the symbol is used for programming the barcode reader. Every symbol of a Macro PDF417 sequence for reader programming is given it. It is not available with the raw option.

Examples

A compact symbol with four columns:

Data:    A truncated PDF417
Options: columns=4
Encoder: pdf417compact

QR Code

The QR Code symbology is a 2D matrix-style barcode symbology that can encode full 256 character extended-ASCII.

Also known as: Quick Response Code.

Uses:

  • Content for phones: web links, Wi-Fi network details, contact cards, email, phone numbers, text messages, locations and calendar events.
  • SEPA credit transfers (EPC QR Code, also known as GiroCode).
  • Mobile airline boarding passes (IATA Bar Coded Boarding Pass).
  • Unit packets and aggregated packaging of tobacco products under EU traceability Regulation (EU) 2018/574, with error correction level H.
  • Merchant payment QR codes to the EMVCo QR Code Specification, such as Brazil's Pix (EMV QR Code).
  • Automotive transport labels (Global Transport Label: Odette, AIAG B-16, VDA 4994).

Variants:

  • Micro QR Code is a small QR Code that is used in applications that require a small symbol space.
  • Rectangular Micro QR Code is a rectangular variant that provides a compact symbol suitable for narrow, elongated spaces.
  • GS1 QR Code is a variant that should be used when encoding data that is in GS1 Application Identifier standard format.
  • GS1 Digital Link QR Code is a variant that should be used when encoding a GS1 Digital Link URI.
  • HIBC QR Code is a variant of QR Code that should be used when encoding HIBC formatted data.
  • Swiss QR Code is a variant of the QR Code for use with the QR-bill application supporting Swiss payments.
  • EPC QR Code is a variant of QR Code carrying the details of a SEPA credit transfer.
  • EMV QR Code is a variant of QR Code carrying EMV merchant-presented payment data.

Standards: ISO/IEC 18004, JIS X 0510, ITS - QR Code, AIM ISS - QR Code.

Data and Options

  • The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1. When supported by the receiver characters from other code pages can be encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • When the parsefnc option is specified, non-data function characters can be specified by escape sequences:
    • ^FNC1: FNC1. Recommendation: Consider GS1 QR Code for encoding GS1 AI syntax data.
    • ^ECI000000 to ^ECI999999: ECI indicators
    • ^FNC@: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g. ^FNC@T... or ^FNC@99.... See FNC1 in second position.
    • An FNC1 before any data, or FNC1 in second position, selects FNC1 mode, in which any further FNC1 is a field separator. Without FNC1 mode an FNC1 after data cannot be encoded.
    • ECIs are not available with FNC1 in first or second position.
  • The eclevel option is used to specify the error correction level:
    • eclevel=L - Low
    • eclevel=M - Medium (default)
    • eclevel=Q - Quality
    • eclevel=H - High
    • A higher level lets the symbol be read with more of it damaged, such as by wear or by a logo printed over its centre, at the cost of a larger symbol. Some applications fix the level, such as M for an EPC QR Code or a Swiss QR-bill, and H for unit packets of tobacco under Regulation (EU) 2018/574.
  • The fixedeclevel option will prevent the error correction level from being opportunistically raised when a better fit to the current matrix is possible.
  • The version option is used to specify the size of the symbol, 1 to 40.
  • If unspecified the encoder will select the version of the symbol that is the minimum size to represent the given data at the selected error correction level.
  • The mask option is used to specify the mask pattern, 1 to 8. If unspecified the encoder selects the best mask.
  • The sampos, samtotal and samparity options make the symbol one of a Structured Append sequence of 2 to 16 symbols, which a reader reassembles into a single message. All three are required:
    • sampos is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to samtotal.
    • samtotal is the number of symbols in the sequence.
    • samparity is the parity of the whole message, from 0 to 255, and is the same in every symbol of the sequence. It is the XOR of the bytes of the message, and is reported by the encoder for the data that it encodes (see Developing a Frontend to BWIPP), so the parity of a message is the XOR of the parities reported for its parts.
    • Structured Append is not available for Micro QR Code, Rectangular Micro QR Code, GS1 QR Code, GS1 Digital Link QR Code, Swiss QR Code, EPC QR Code or EMV QR Code symbols.
  • Deprecated: The suppresskanjimode option will prevent the use of Kanji Mode internal encodation. Some readers erroneously consider a Kanji Mode section as an indication that the affected part of the message should be interpreted using a Shift-JIS character set rather than as a data compaction strategy. There's nothing that can be done other than to disable the use of Kanji Mode data compaction for symbols intended to be read by such broken readers.
  • Deprecated: The format option is used to specify the symbol type, either:
    • full (default)
    • micro: Consider Micro QR Code for Micro QR Code symbols.
    • rmqr: Consider Rectangular Micro QR Code for rMQR symbols.

Common Content

Phones recognise the following formats, which are conventions documented by ZXing rather than part of the QR Code standard:

Content Data
Web link https://example.com/
Wi-Fi network WIFI:T:WPA;S:network;P:password;; with T one of WEP, WPA (which also serves WPA2 personal networks), WPA2-EAP or nopass, and H:true added for a hidden network. In the network name and password, \, ;, ,, " and : are each preceded by \.
Email mailto:someone@example.com
Phone number tel:+12125551212
Text message sms:+18005551212:Message (SMSTO: is also seen)
Location geo:40.71872,-73.98905,100 (latitude, longitude and optionally altitude)
Contact MECARD:N:Owen,Sean;TEL:12125551212;EMAIL:srowen@example.com;;, or a vCard from BEGIN:VCARD to END:VCARD
Calendar event An iCalendar event from BEGIN:VEVENT to END:VEVENT

The European Payments Council's EPC QR Code, also known as GiroCode, which initiates a SEPA credit transfer, is available as the EPC QR Code variant, which validates its data.

Examples

Identical symbols, the latter using the parse option:

Data:    QR Code
Options:
Encoder: qrcode
Data:    QR ^067ode
Options: parse
Encoder: qrcode

A fixed-size symbol with increased error correction:

Data:    QR CODE 1234
Options: version=10 eclevel=Q
Encoder: qrcode

Micro QR Code

The Micro QR Code symbology is a smaller variant of QR Code that is used in applications that require a small symbol space.

Also known as: Micro Quick Response Code.

Uses:

  • Small items where a full QR Code does not fit, such as small parts and electronic components.

Variants:

  • QR Code is the more popular, larger variant.
  • Rectangular Micro QR Code is a rectangular variant that provides a compact symbol suitable for narrow, elongated spaces.

Standards: ISO/IEC 18004, JIS X 0510, ITS - QR Code, AIM ISS - QR Code.

Data and Options

  • The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
  • An appropriate size will be selected to work around the following restrictions:
    • An M1 symbol is only compatible with numeric data.
    • An M2 symbol is only compatible with numeric and alphanumeric data.
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • The version option is used to specify the size of the symbol, either version=M1, version=M2, version=M3 or version=M4.
  • The eclevel option is used to specify the error correction level:
    • eclevel=L - Low (default)
    • eclevel=M - Medium; Not compatible with M1 symbols
    • eclevel=Q - Quality; Only compatible with M4 symbols
  • The fixedeclevel option will prevent the error correction level from being opportunistically raised when a better fit to the current matrix is possible.
  • If unspecified the encoder will select the version of the symbol that is the minimum size to represent the given data at the selected error correction level.
  • The mask option is used to specify the mask pattern, 1 to 4. If unspecified the encoder selects the best mask.
  • Deprecated: The suppresskanjimode option will prevent the use of Kanji Mode internal encodation. Some readers erroneously consider a Kanji Mode section as an indication that the affected part of the message should be interpreted using a Shift-JIS character set rather than as a data compaction strategy.

Examples

A basic symbol encoding numeric data:

Data:    01234567
Options:
Encoder: microqrcode

Rectangular Micro QR Code

The Rectangular Micro QR Code (rMQR) symbology is a rectangular variant of QR Code that provides a compact symbol suitable for applications where a narrow, elongated symbol is required, such as labels and small cylindrical items.

Also known as: rMQR.

Uses:

  • Long, narrow spaces, such as the edges and margins of boxes and labels.

Variants:

  • QR Code is the more popular, larger square variant.
  • Micro QR Code is a smaller square variant.

Standards: ISO/IEC 23941.

Data and Options

  • The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1. When supported by the receiver characters from other code pages can be encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • When the parsefnc option is specified, non-data function characters can be specified by escape sequences:
    • ^FNC1: FNC1. Recommendation: Consider GS1 QR Code with an R version for encoding GS1 AI syntax data.
    • ^ECI000000 to ^ECI999999: ECI indicators
    • ^FNC@: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g. ^FNC@T... or ^FNC@99.... See FNC1 in second position.
    • An FNC1 before any data, or FNC1 in second position, selects FNC1 mode, in which any further FNC1 is a field separator. Without FNC1 mode an FNC1 after data cannot be encoded.
  • The version option is required and specifies the size of the symbol in RHxW format, where H is the height and W is the width in modules:
    • R7x43, R7x59, R7x77, R7x99, R7x139
    • R9x43, R9x59, R9x77, R9x99, R9x139
    • R11x27, R11x43, R11x59, R11x77, R11x99, R11x139
    • R13x27, R13x43, R13x59, R13x77, R13x99, R13x139
    • R15x43, R15x59, R15x77, R15x99, R15x139
    • R17x43, R17x59, R17x77, R17x99, R17x139
  • The eclevel option is used to specify the error correction level:
    • eclevel=M - Medium (default)
    • eclevel=H - High
  • The fixedeclevel option will prevent the error correction level from being opportunistically raised when a better fit to the selected symbol is possible.
  • Deprecated: The suppresskanjimode option will prevent the use of Kanji Mode internal encodation. Some readers erroneously consider a Kanji Mode section as an indication that the affected part of the message should be interpreted using a Shift-JIS character set rather than as a data compaction strategy.

Examples

A numeric-only symbol:

Data:    1234
Options: version=R17x139
Encoder: rectangularmicroqrcode

A Figure 1 example symbol from the specification:

Data:    12345678901234567890123456
Options: version=R13x27 eclevel=M fixedeclevel
Encoder: rectangularmicroqrcode

An alphanumeric symbol:

Data:    AC-42
Options: version=R7x59 eclevel=H fixedeclevel
Encoder: rectangularmicroqrcode

A symbol with ECI:

Data:    ^ECI000009^161^162^163^164^165
Options: parse parsefnc version=R17x139 eclevel=M fixedeclevel
Encoder: rectangularmicroqrcode

Swiss QR Code

Swiss QR Code is a variant of the QR Code barcode symbology for use with the QR-bill application supporting Swiss payments.

Uses:

  • Swiss and Liechtenstein payment slips (QR-bill).

Standards: Swiss Implementation Guidelines QR-bill, ISO/IEC 18004, ITS - QR Code.

Data and Options

  • The data field input is provided in the format described in the Swiss Implementation Guidelines QR-bill document.
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • The version option is used to specify the size of the symbol. This is not typically specified.
  • If the version is unspecified the encoder will default to creating a symbol that is the minimum size to represent the given data at error correction level M, which the Swiss Implementation Guidelines require.
  • Deprecated: The suppresskanjimode option will prevent the use of Kanji Mode internal encodation. Some readers erroneously consider a Kanji Mode section as an indication that the affected part of the message should be interpreted using a Shift-JIS character set rather than as a data compaction strategy.

Note: The symbol is drawn 46mm x 46mm, excluding the quiet zone, whatever its version, with a 7mm x 7mm Swiss Cross over its centre.

Examples

A QR-bill payment with structured creditor reference:

Data:    SPC^010\
         0200^010\
         1^010\
         CH5800791123000889012^010\
         S^010\
         Robert Schneider AG^010\
         Rue du Lac^010\
         1268^010\
         2501^010\
         Biel^010\
         CH^010\
         ^010\
         ^010\
         ^010\
         ^010\
         ^010\
         ^010\
         ^010\
         199.95^010\
         CHF^010\
         S^010\
         Pia-Maria Rutschmann-Schnyder^010\
         Grosse Marktgasse^010\
         28^010\
         9400^010\
         Rorschach^010\
         CH^010\
         SCOR^010\
         RF18539007547034^010\
         ^010\
         EPD
Options: parse
Encoder: swissqrcode

EPC QR Code

EPC QR Code is a variant of the QR Code barcode symbology carrying the details of a SEPA credit transfer, so that a payer can initiate the payment by scanning it, for example from an invoice. It is also known as the GiroCode.

Uses:

  • Payments in euro across the Single Euro Payments Area.

Standards: EPC069-12 Quick Response Code - Guidelines to Enable the Data Capture for the Initiation of a SEPA Credit Transfer, ISO/IEC 18004, ITS - QR Code.

Data and Options

  • The data field input is the payload described in the EPC guidelines: up to 12 elements separated by line feeds (or carriage return and line feed), in this order, with nothing after the last element given:
    • Service Tag, BCD.
    • Version, 001 or 002.
    • Character set of the elements that follow: 1 UTF-8, 2 ISO 8859-1, 3 ISO 8859-2, 4 ISO 8859-4, 5 ISO 8859-5, 6 ISO 8859-7, 7 ISO 8859-10, 8 ISO 8859-15.
    • Identification, SCT.
    • The BIC of the beneficiary's bank, of 8 or 11 characters, which may be empty in version 002.
    • The name of the beneficiary, up to 70 characters.
    • The IBAN of the beneficiary's account.
    • Optionally the amount: EUR followed by an amount from 0.01 to 999999999.99.
    • Optionally the purpose: a code of up to 4 characters.
    • Optionally either a structured creditor reference of up to 35 characters, such as an ISO 11649 RF reference, or remittance text of up to 140 characters, but not both.
    • Optionally information for the payer, up to 70 characters.
  • The encoder validates the elements, including the check digits of the IBAN and of an RF creditor reference. The whole payload must not exceed 331 bytes.
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying the line feeds as ^010 and other characters.
  • The symbol is created at error correction level M, which the EPC guidelines require.

Examples

A payment with an amount and a structured creditor reference:

Data:    BCD^010\
         001^010\
         1^010\
         SCT^010\
         BHBLDEHHXXX^010\
         Franz Mustermann^010\
         DE71110220330123456789^010\
         EUR12.3^010\
         GDDS^010\
         RF18539007547034
Options: parse
Encoder: epcqrcode

A version 002 payment without a BIC, with information for the payer:

Data:    BCD^010\
         002^010\
         1^010\
         SCT^010\
         ^010\
         Harbour Choir^010\
         DE89370400440532013000^010\
         EUR12.50^010\
         ^010\
         ^010\
         ^010\
         Donation
Options: parse
Encoder: epcqrcode

EMV QR Code

EMV QR Code is a variant of the QR Code barcode symbology that carries the merchant-presented payment data of the EMV QR Code Specification for Payment Systems, which is the basis of national payment QR codes such as Pix (Brazil), Bharat QR (India), PayNow (Singapore), PromptPay (Thailand), DuitNow (Malaysia), QRIS (Indonesia) and KE-QR (Kenya).

Standards: EMV QR Code Specification for Payment Systems (EMV QRCPS) - Merchant-Presented Mode; ISO/IEC 18004.

Data and Options

  • The data field is the payload of data objects, each a two-digit ID, a two-digit length and a value of that many characters, beginning with the Payload Format Indicator 000201 and ending with the CRC object 6304 and its four upper case hexadecimal digits.
  • If the CRC object is omitted then the encoder will calculate and add it. If it is given then it is verified.
  • The encoder validates the data objects of the specification:
    • Each ID appears at most once, and IDs 65 to 79 are reserved.
    • At least one Merchant Account Information object, IDs 02 to 51, is present, and the templates 26 to 51 and 80 to 99 begin with a Globally Unique Identifier.
    • The Merchant Category Code (52), Transaction Currency (53), Country Code (58), Merchant Name (59) and Merchant City (60) are present and well formed.
    • The Point of Initiation Method (01), Transaction Amount (54), Tip or Convenience Indicator with its fixed or percentage fee (55 to 57), Postal Code (61), Additional Data Field Template (62) and Merchant Information Language Template (64) are well formed when present.
  • The alternate language template may contain UTF-8 text, whose lengths count characters.
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent byte value.
  • The options of QR Code, such as eclevel, are available, except for Structured Append.

Examples

A static merchant code, with the CRC calculated by the encoder:

Data:    00020101021126310015COM.EXAMPLE.PAY0108123456785204581253038405802US5913CORNER BAKERY6009SPRINGTON
Options:
Encoder: emvqrcode

One-Dimensional

Code 128

Code 128 is an arbitrarily long, high-density barcode symbology that can be used to encode full 256 character extended-ASCII.

Also known as: USD-6, USS-128, Code 128A, Code 128B, Code 128C.

Uses:

  • Identifiers outside the GS1 system, such as carrier tracking numbers and warehouse, bin, inventory and asset labels.
  • Amazon FNSKU product labels.
  • Aggregated packaging of tobacco products under EU traceability Regulation (EU) 2018/574.
  • Blood, tissue and cell products labelled to ISBT 128.
  • International registered mail, parcels and EMS, carrying the UPU S10 tracking number.
  • DPD parcel labels (DPD Parcel Label).
  • Clinical laboratory specimen tubes (CLSI AUTO02).
  • Automotive transport labels (Global Transport Label: Odette, AIAG B-16, VDA 4994).

Variants:

  • GS1-128 is a variant of Code 128 that should be used when encoding data that is in GS1 Application Identifier standard format.
  • HIBC Code 128 is a variant of Code 128 that should be used when encoding HIBC formatted data.
  • UPU S10 is a variant of Code 128 carrying the S10 identifier of a postal item.
  • DPD Parcel Label is a variant of Code 128 on the parcel labels of DPD.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15417, ANSI/AIM BC4 - ISS Code 128, BS EN 799.

Data and Options

  • The data field can consist of any extended ASCII data. The default interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
  • The mandatory check digit is calculated automatically.
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII or extended-ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters, e.g. ^029 for GS, ^209 for Ñ, etc.
  • FNC4 function characters will be inserted automatically to allow the encoding of extended ASCII characters.
  • When the parsefnc option is specified, non-data function characters can be specified by escape sequences:
    • ^FNC1: FNC1. Recommendation: Consider GS1-128 for encoding GS1 AI syntax data.
    • ^FNC@: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g. ^FNC@T... or ^FNC@99.... See FNC1 in second position. The human readable text leaves out this FNC1.
    • ^FNC2: FNC2
    • ^FNC3: FNC3
  • Deprecated: The raw option denotes that the data field is providing the input as pre-encoded codewords in ^NNN format, suitable for direct low-level encoding. You can use the alttext option to specify human-readable text.
  • Deprecated: For internal use. When the parsefnc option is specified, the special pseudo characters ^LNKA and ^LNKC at the end of the symbol indicate that a GS1-128 symbol includes a CC-A/B or CC-C GS1 composite 2D component.

Examples

A symbol encoding alphanumeric data:

Data:    Count0123456789!
Options: includetext
Encoder: code128

Code 39

The Code 39 barcode symbology is discrete, variable length and self-checking.

Also known as: Code 3 of 9, Alpha39, USD-3, USS-39.

Uses:

  • Asset and inventory labels.
  • US military shipping labels and container markings (LOGMARS, MIL-STD-129).
  • Vehicle Identification Numbers (VIN).
  • Automotive trading-partner labels (AIAG B-10), each field carrying its Data Identifier.
  • European automotive goods labels (Odette Transport Label, VDA 4902).

Variants:

  • Code 39 Extended is a variant of Code 39 that can be used to encode full 128 character ASCII with the use of shift character combinations.
  • HIBC Code 39 is a variant of Code 39 that should be used when encoding HIBC formatted data.
  • LOGMARS is the use of Code 39 by the US Department of Defense.
  • VIN is a variant of Code 39 carrying a Vehicle Identification Number.
  • Codablock A is a stacked symbology whose rows are Code 39 symbols.
  • AIM USD-2 is a subset of Code 39 containing the characters A-Z, 0-9, space, - and ..

Standards: ISO/IEC 16388, ANSI/AIM BC1 - USS Code 39, BS EN 800, MIL-STD-1189.

Data and Options

  • The data field can hold any of the following:
    • Numbers 0-9
    • Capital letters A-Z
    • Symbols -.$/+% and space
  • The includecheck option calculates the check digit.
  • The validatecheck option takes the last character of the data to be the check character and refuses the data if it is wrong.
  • The includecheckintext option makes the calculated check digit appear in the human readable text.
  • The hidestars option suppresses the asterisks in the human readable text.

Examples

A basic symbol:

Data:    CODE39
Options: includetext
Encoder: code39

A symbol with a check digit:

Data:    CODE39
Options: includecheck includetext includecheckintext
Encoder: code39

A symbol with the asterisks hidden from the text:

Data:    CODE39
Options: hidestars includecheck includetext
Encoder: code39

Code 39 Extended

The Code 39 Extended barcode symbology is discrete, variable length and self-checking. It is based on Code 39 but can encode full 128 character ASCII by using shift combinations.

Also known as: Code 39 Full ASCII.

Uses:

  • Code 39 labels that need lowercase letters or other ASCII characters, read by scanners set to Full ASCII.

Variants:

  • Code 39 is a simpler variant of Code 39 Extended.

Standards: ISO/IEC 16388, ANSI/AIM BC1 - USS Code 39, BS EN 800.

Data and Options

  • The data field can consist of any ASCII data.
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters, e.g. ^029 for GS, etc.
  • The includecheck option calculates the check digit.
  • The validatecheck option takes the last character of the data to be the check character, calculated over the shift-encoded Code 39 characters, and refuses the data if it is wrong.
  • The includecheckintext option makes the calculated check digit appear in the human readable text.
  • The hidestars option suppresses the asterisks in the human readable text.

Examples

A symbol encoding lowercase and special characters:

Data:    Code39 Ext!
Options: includetext includecheck
Encoder: code39ext

A symbol using the parse option to encode a GS control character:

Data:    Code39^029Extended
Options: parse includecheck
Encoder: code39ext

Code 93

Code 93 is a continuous, variable length, self-checking barcode symbology.

Also known as: USD-7, USS-93.

Variants:

  • Code 93 Extended is a variant of Code 93 that can be used to encode full 128 character ASCII with the use of special shift character combinations.

Standards: ANSI/AIM BC5 - USS Code 93, ITS 93i.

Data and Options

  • The data field can hold any of the following:
    • Numbers 0-9
    • Capital letters A-Z
    • Symbols -.$/+% and space
  • The includecheck option calculates the two check digits.
  • The validatecheck option takes the last two characters of the data to be the check characters C and K and refuses the data if they are wrong. A check character that is a shift character is given as ^SFT$, ^SFT%, ^SFT/ or ^SFT+ with parsefnc.
  • Deprecated: For internal use. The parsefnc option allows the special shift characters to be supplied as escape sequences:
    • ^SFT$: ($)
    • ^SFT%: (%)
    • ^SFT/: (/)
    • ^SFT+: (+)

Examples

A basic symbol:

Data:    CODE93
Options: includecheck
Encoder: code93

A symbol including a special shift combination (/)A representing !:

Data:    CODE93^SFT/A
Options: parsefnc includecheck
Encoder: code93

Code 93 Extended

The Code 93 Extended barcode symbology is continuous, variable length and self-checking. It is based on Code 93 but can encode full 128 character ASCII using four additional shift characters: ($) (%) (/) (+)

Also known as: Code 93 Full ASCII.

Variants:

  • Code 93 is a simpler variant of the Code 93 Extended barcode symbology.

Standards: ANSI/AIM BC5 - USS Code 93, ITS 93i.

Data and Options

  • The data field can consist of any ASCII data.
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters, e.g. ^029 for GS, etc.
  • The includecheck option calculates the two check digits.
  • The validatecheck option is not available, since the check characters need not be ASCII characters.

Examples

A symbol encoding lowercase and special characters:

Data:    Code93Ext!
Options: includecheck
Encoder: code93ext

A symbol using the parse option to encode a GS control character:

Data:    Code93^029Extended
Options: parse includecheck
Encoder: code93ext

Interleaved 2 of 5
