Interleaved 2 of 5 is a high-density numeric barcode symbology.

Also known as: ITF, Code 2 of 5 Interleaved, USD-1, USS-Interleaved 2 of 5.

Uses:

  • Brazilian bank payment slips (boleto bancário), carrying the 44-digit payment code.
  • Numeric identifiers on cartons and in warehousing; for the GTIN of a case, ITF-14 is its GS1 form.

Variants:

  • ITF-14 is a variant of Interleaved 2 of 5 that should be used when encoding a fourteen-digit GTIN.
  • Deutsche Post Identcode is a variant of Interleaved 2 of 5 that is used by Deutsche Post to identify parcels.
  • Deutsche Post Leitcode is a variant of Interleaved 2 of 5 that is used by Deutsche Post to carry a parcel's routing code.

Standards: ISO/IEC 16390, ANSI/AIM BC2 - USS Interleaved 2 of 5, BS EN 801.

Data and Options

  • The data can consist of any number of digits.
  • If the length of the symbol including the possible check digit would be odd then the data is prefixed by 0.
  • The includecheck option calculates the check digit.
  • The validatecheck option takes the last digit of the data to be the check digit and refuses the data if it is wrong.
  • The includecheckintext option makes the calculated checksum appear in the human readable text.

Examples

A basic symbol:

Data:    0123456789
Options:
Encoder: interleaved2of5

A symbol with a check digit:

Data:    2401234567
Options: includecheck includetext includecheckintext
Encoder: interleaved2of5

Supply Chain

EAN-14

EAN-14 is an implementation of the GS1-128 barcode symbology with AI (01) that is used to encode a lone GTIN-14.

Note: EAN-14 is a colloquial term used to describe a GS1-128 barcode symbol containing only a GTIN.

Also known as: GS1-128 without attribute data.

Misnomers: UCC-14.

Uses:

  • The GTIN of a trade item grouping, such as a case or carton, alone on a GS1 logistic label.

Data syntax: GS1 Application Identifiers.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15417, ANSI/AIM BC4-1999 ISS, BS EN 799, GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data field input must be a solitary AI (01) with thirteen or fourteen digits of a GTIN, i.e. (01)....
  • Arbitrary spacing may be placed between the digits to format the human readable text without interfering with the encoded data.
  • If thirteen digits of primary data are supplied then the check digit is calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided check digit will be verified.
  • With strictspec, the ast option takes the GS1-128 application standards, such as ast=gs1.sst2 for trade items scanned in general distribution.

Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

Data:    (01)09528765432108
Options: includetext
Encoder: ean14
Data:    (01)0952876543210
Options: includetext
Encoder: ean14

ITF-14

ITF-14 is an implementation of the Interleaved 2 of 5 barcode symbology that is typically used to encode a GTIN-14, GTIN-13 or GTIN-12.

Also known as: UPC Shipping Container Symbol, SCS, UPC Case Code.

Uses:

  • The GTIN of outer cases and cartons of trade items in distribution, often printed directly onto corrugated board.

Standards: ISO/IEC 16390, ANSI/AIM BC2 - USS Interleaved 2 of 5, BS EN 801, GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data consists of either thirteen or fourteen digits.
  • Arbitrary spacing may be placed between the digits to format the human readable text without interfering with the encoded data.
  • If thirteen digits are supplied then the check digit is calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided check digit will be verified.
  • A bearer frame surrounding the symbol and its quiet zones is drawn by default (showborder). The GS1 General Specifications require one, with a nominal thickness of 4.83 mm, when the symbol is printed using printing plates, typically directly onto corrugated board. The borderwidth option sets its thickness.
  • The showbearer option draws bearer bars at the top and bottom only, in place of the frame, as allowed when the symbol is printed without printing plates.

Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

Data:    09528765432108
Options: includetext
Encoder: itf14
Data:    0952876543210
Options: includetext
Encoder: itf14

SSCC-18

SSCC-18 is an implementation of the GS1-128 barcode symbology with AI (00) that is typically used to encode a lone eighteen-digit shipping container serial number.

Note: SSCC-18 is a colloquial term used to describe a GS1-128 barcode symbol containing only an SSCC.

Also known as: NVE.

Misnomers: EAN-18.

Uses:

  • The SSCC alone on the logistic (shipping) label of a pallet or other logistic unit.

Data syntax: GS1 Application Identifiers.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15417, ANSI/AIM BC4-1999 ISS, BS EN 799, GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data field input must be a solitary AI (00) with seventeen or eighteen digits of a Serial Shipping Container Code, i.e. (00)....
  • Arbitrary spacing may be placed between the digits to format the human readable text without interfering with the encoded data.
  • If seventeen digits of primary data are supplied then the check digit is calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided check digit will be verified.
  • With strictspec, the ast option takes the GS1-128 application standards, such as ast=gs1.sst5 for a logistic label.

Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

Data:    (00)095287654321012346
Options: includetext
Encoder: sscc18
Data:    (00)09528765432101234
Options: includetext
Encoder: sscc18

GS1 DataMatrix

GS1 DataMatrix is an implementation of the Data Matrix (ECC 200) barcode symbology with GS1 formatted data.

Uses:

  • Healthcare: human and veterinary pharmaceutical (drug) packs (including the EU Falsified Medicines Directive and the US Drug Supply Chain Security Act) and medical devices (UDI).
  • Direct part marking, such as by laser, chemical etching or dot peen.
  • Retail point of sale in 2D, one of the symbols that GS1 US's Sunrise 2027 initiative aims for scanners to read.
  • Unit packets and aggregated packaging of tobacco products under EU traceability Regulation (EU) 2018/574.
  • Patient wristbands and staff identification in hospitals (GSRN).
  • Logistic (shipping) labels, beside the GS1-128 barcode or alone on small logistic units.
  • Returnable and individual assets (GRAI, GIAI).

Variants:

  • GS1 DataMatrix Rectangular is equivalent to using format=rectangle.
  • GS1 Digital Link Data Matrix encodes GS1 data as a Digital Link URI.

Data syntax: GS1 Application Identifiers.

Standards: ISO/IEC 16022, ANSI/AIM BC11 - ISS Data Matrix, GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data field input is provided in GS1 Application Identifier standard format.
  • Note that it is not necessary to specify FNC1 characters since the encoder will insert these automatically where necessary.
  • Deprecated. The dontlint option disables GS1 Application Identifier syntax validation allowing images to be generated for input that does not comply with GS1 standards.
  • The format option is used to specify the shape of the symbol, either square (default) or rectangle.
  • The columns and rows options are used to specify the size of the symbol.
  • The version option can also be used to specify the symbol size, as version=RxC. Valid options are:
    • With format=square: 10x10, 12x12, 14x14, 16x16, 18x18, 20x20, 22x22, 24x24, 26x26, 32x32, 36x36, 40x40, 44x44, 48x48, 52x52, 64x64, 72x72, 80x80, 88x88, 96x96, 104x104, 120x120, 132x132, 144x144
    • With format=rectangle: 8x18, 8x32, 12x26, 12x36, 16x36, 16x48
  • If columns, rows and version are unspecified the encoder will default to creating a symbol of the specified format that is the minimum size to represent the given data.
  • With strictspec, the ast option sizes the symbol to a GS1 application standard, such as:
    • ast=gs1.sst6 - healthcare primary packaging, such as a blister or vial
    • ast=gs1.sst8 - healthcare packs also scanned in general distribution
    • ast=gs1.sst10 - healthcare packs dispensed to the patient, such as an outer pack carrying the EU Falsified Medicines Directive's unique identifier
    • ast=gs1.sst7.dpm.a - direct part marking with a connected finder pattern, such as by laser or chemical etching
    • ast=gs1.sst7.dpm.b - direct part marking with separate modules, such as by dot peen
    • ast=gs1.sst12.trade, ast=gs1.sst12.group - tobacco unit packets, and aggregated packaging

Examples

GTIN 9521234543213; Weight 0.123kg:

Data:    (01)09521234543213(3103)000123
Options:
Encoder: gs1datamatrix

GS1 DataMatrix Rectangular

GTIN 9521234543213; Expiration date; Batch; Ship to location:

Data:    (01)09521234543213(17)120508(10)ABCD1234(410)9501101020917
Options:
Encoder: gs1datamatrixrectangular

GS1 QR Code

GS1 QR Code is an implementation of the QR Code barcode symbology with GS1 formatted data.

Uses:

  • Logistic (shipping) labels, beside the GS1-128 barcode or alone on small logistic units.
  • Unit packets and aggregated packaging of tobacco products under EU traceability Regulation (EU) 2018/574.
  • Returnable and individual assets (GRAI, GIAI).
  • Direct part marking of items other than medical devices.

Variants:

  • GS1 Digital Link QR Code encodes GS1 data as a Digital Link URI.

Data syntax: GS1 Application Identifiers.

Standards: ISO/IEC 18004, ITS - QR Code, GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data field input is provided in GS1 Application Identifier standard format.
  • Note that it is not necessary to specify FNC1 characters since the encoder will insert these automatically where necessary.
  • Deprecated. The dontlint option disables GS1 Application Identifier syntax validation allowing images to be generated for input that does not comply with GS1 standards.
  • The eclevel option is used to specify the error correction level:
    • eclevel=L - Low
    • eclevel=M - Medium (default)
    • eclevel=Q - Quality
    • eclevel=H - High
  • The fixedeclevel option will prevent the error correction level from being opportunistically raised when a better fit to the current matrix is possible.
  • The version option is used to specify the size of the symbol, 1 to 40.
  • If the version is unspecified the encoder will default to creating a symbol that is the minimum size to represent the given data at the selected error correction level.
  • With strictspec, the ast option sizes the symbol to a GS1 application standard, such as ast=gs1.sst12.trade for tobacco unit packets (with eclevel=H) and ast=gs1.sst12.group for aggregated packaging.

Examples

GTIN 9521234543213; Extended packaging URL:

Data:    (01)09521234543213(8200)http://www.abc.net
Options:
Encoder: gs1qrcode

GTIN 9521234543213; Extended packaging URL; Batch; Ship to location:

Data:    (01)09521234543213(8200)http://abc.net(10)XYZ(410)9501101020917
Options:
Encoder: gs1qrcode

GS1 Digital Link Data Matrix

GS1 Digital Link Data Matrix is an implementation of the Data Matrix (ECC 200) barcode symbology containing a GS1 Digital Link URI.

Uses:

  • Products whose 2D code a point-of-sale scanner reads for the GTIN and a phone opens as a web page (GS1 Digital Link).

Variants:

  • GS1 DataMatrix encodes GS1 data in Application Identifier format.

Data syntax: GS1 Digital Link URI.

Standards: ISO/IEC 16022, ANSI/AIM BC11 - ISS Data Matrix, GS1 Digital Link Standard: URI Syntax.

Data and Options

  • The data field input is provided as a GS1 Digital Link URI.
  • The includetext option enables the display of HRI.
  • Deprecated. The dontlint option disables GS1 Application Identifier syntax validation allowing images to be generated for input that does not comply with GS1 standards.
  • The format option is used to specify the shape of the symbol, either square (default) or rectangle.
  • The columns and rows options are used to specify the size of the symbol.
  • The version option can also be used to specify the symbol size, as version=RxC. Valid options are:
    • With format=square: 10x10, 12x12, 14x14, 16x16, 18x18, 20x20, 22x22, 24x24, 26x26, 32x32, 36x36, 40x40, 44x44, 48x48, 52x52, 64x64, 72x72, 80x80, 88x88, 96x96, 104x104, 120x120, 132x132, 144x144
    • With format=rectangle: 8x18, 8x32, 12x26, 12x36, 16x36, 16x48
  • If columns, rows and version are unspecified the encoder will default to creating a symbol of the specified format that is the minimum size to represent the given data.

Examples

A GS1 Digital Link URI containing GTIN and additional data:

Data:    https://id.gs1.org/01/09521234543213/22/ABC%2d123?99=XYZ%2f987
Options:
Encoder: gs1dldatamatrix

With human readable interpretation:

Data:    https://id.gs1.org/01/09521234543213/22/ABC%2d123?99=XYZ%2f987
Options: includetext
Encoder: gs1dldatamatrix

Note: By default, the HRI displays only the primary key extracted from the Digital Link URI.

With full AI extraction into multiline HRI:

Data:    https://id.gs1.org/01/09521234543213/10/ABC123/21/12345
Options: includetext alttext=GTIN~~~~~~(01)~09521234543213|BATCH/LOT~(10)~ABC123|SERIAL~~~~(21)~12345
         alttextsubspace=~ alttextsplit=| textxalign=offright textxoffset=3
         textyalign=center textfont=Courier
Encoder: gs1dldatamatrix

GS1 Digital Link QR Code

GS1 Digital Link QR Code is an implementation of the QR Code barcode symbology containing a GS1 Digital Link URI.

Uses:

  • Retail product packaging that a phone opens as a web page and a 2D point-of-sale scanner reads for the GTIN, one of the symbols that GS1 US's Sunrise 2027 initiative aims for scanners to read. Until they do, products usually also carry their EAN/UPC barcode.

Variants:

  • GS1 QR Code encodes GS1 data in Application Identifier format.

Data syntax: GS1 Digital Link URI.

Standards: ISO/IEC 18004, ITS - QR Code, GS1 Digital Link Standard: URI Syntax.

Data and Options

  • The data field input is provided as a GS1 Digital Link URI.
  • The includetext option enables the display of HRI.
  • Deprecated. The dontlint option disables GS1 Application Identifier syntax validation allowing images to be generated for input that does not comply with GS1 standards.
  • The eclevel option is used to specify the error correction level:
    • eclevel=L - Low
    • eclevel=M - Medium (default)
    • eclevel=Q - Quality
    • eclevel=H - High
  • The fixedeclevel option will prevent the error correction level from being opportunistically raised when a better fit to the current matrix is possible.
  • The version option is used to specify the size of the symbol, 1 to 40.
  • If the version is unspecified the encoder will default to creating a symbol that is the minimum size to represent the given data at the selected error correction level.

Examples

A GS1 Digital Link URI containing GTIN and additional data:

Data:    https://id.gs1.org/01/09521234543213/22/ABC%2d123?99=XYZ%2f987
Options:
Encoder: gs1dlqrcode

With human readable interpretation:

Data:    https://id.gs1.org/01/09521234543213/22/ABC%2d123?99=XYZ%2f987
Options: includetext
Encoder: gs1dlqrcode

Note: By default, the HRI displays only the primary key extracted from the Digital Link URI.

With full AI extraction into multiline HRI:

Data:    https://id.gs1.org/01/09521234543213/10/ABC123/21/12345
Options: includetext alttext=(01)~09521234543213|(10)~ABC123|(21)~12345
         alttextsubspace=~ alttextsplit=| textxalign=offright textxoffset=5
         textyalign=center
Encoder: gs1dlqrcode

With a "P.o.S. ready" brand:

Data:    https://id.gs1.org/01/09521234543213/22/ABC%2d123?99=XYZ%2f987
Options: includetext extratext=P.o.S.~ready extratextsubspace=~
         extratextfont=Helvetica extratextsize=5 extratextyoffset=5
Encoder: gs1dlqrcode

GS1-128

GS1-128 is an implementation of the Code 128 barcode symbology which carries GS1 formatted data.

Also known as: UCC/EAN-128, EAN-128, UCC-128.

Uses:

  • GS1 logistic labels (shipping labels) on pallets, cases and other logistic units, carrying the SSCC and data such as batch or lot numbers, dates and weights.
  • Aggregated packaging of tobacco products under EU traceability Regulation (EU) 2018/574 (GS1 SST 12).
  • Cases and cartons in distribution carrying a batch, an expiry or best-before date, or a weight with the GTIN.
  • Healthcare: pharmaceutical packs and medical devices, including UDI labels.
  • Returnable assets such as kegs, gas cylinders, pallets and crates, and individual assets (GRAI, GIAI).

Variants:

  • GS1-128 Composite is a variant of GS1-128 that should be used when a CC-A, CC-B or CC-C GS1 composite 2D component is required.
  • EAN-14 is a variant of GS1-128 that should be used when encoding a lone fourteen-digit GTIN.
  • SSCC-18 is a variant of GS1-128 that should be used when encoding a lone eighteen-digit SSCC.

Data syntax: GS1 Application Identifiers.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15417, ANSI/AIM BC4-1999 ISS, BS EN 799, GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data field input is provided in GS1 Application Identifier standard format.
  • Note that it is not necessary to specify FNC1 characters since the encoder will insert these automatically where necessary.
  • Deprecated. The dontlint option disables GS1 Application Identifier syntax validation allowing images to be generated for input that does not comply with GS1 standards.
  • Deprecated: For internal use. The linkagea option specifies that the symbol includes a CC-A or CC-B GS1 composite 2D component.
  • Deprecated: For internal use. The linkagec option specifies that the symbol includes a CC-C GS1 composite 2D component.

Examples

GTIN 9521234543213; Weight 0.123kg:

Data:    (01)09521234543213(3103)000123
Options: includetext
Encoder: gs1-128

GTIN 9521234543213; Expiration date 1 January 2010; Batch 123ABC; Serial 1234567890:

Data:    (01)09521234543213(17)100101(10)123ABC(21)1234567890
Options: includetext
Encoder: gs1-128

GS1 DotCode

GS1 DotCode is an implementation of the DotCode barcode symbology with GS1 formatted data.

Uses:

  • Unit packets of tobacco products under EU traceability Regulation (EU) 2018/574.

Variants:

  • DotCode is the base symbology without GS1-specific formatting.

Data syntax: GS1 Application Identifiers.

Standards: AIM - ISS DotCode, GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data field input is provided in GS1 Application Identifier standard format.
  • Note that it is not necessary to specify FNC1 characters since the encoder will insert these automatically where necessary.
  • Deprecated. The dontlint option disables GS1 Application Identifier syntax validation allowing images to be generated for input that does not comply with GS1 standards.
  • The ratio option is used to specify the aspect ratio of the symbol. The default is 1.5.
  • The columns and rows options are used to specify the size of the symbol. When these are not specified a symbol is generated that maintains the selected aspect ratio.
  • With strictspec, the ast option sizes the symbol to a GS1 application standard, such as ast=gs1.sst12.trade for tobacco unit packets.
  • Deprecated: Use only if performance is a concern. The fast option is used to enable the optional high-speed symbol masking algorithm.

Examples

TPX 5vBZIF%!<B;?oa%; GTIN 9521234543213; Production date/time:

Data:    (235)5vBZIF%!<B;?oa%(01)09521234543213(8008)19052001
Options: rows=16
Encoder: gs1dotcode

GS1 DataBar Family

GS1 DataBar Omnidirectional

GS1 DataBar Omnidirectional is a fixed-length, linear barcode symbology that can be used to encode a GTIN-14 for use at point of sale.

Also known as: RSS-14.

Uses:

  • Small retail items scanned at point of sale, such as loose fresh produce.

Variants:

  • GS1 DataBar Stacked Omnidirectional is a variant of GS1 DataBar Omnidirectional for use where a taller, narrower symbol is required.
  • GS1 DataBar Truncated is a variant of GS1 DataBar Omnidirectional of reduced height for items not scanned at point of sale.
  • GS1 DataBar Omnidirectional Composite is a variant of GS1 DataBar Omnidirectional that should be used when a CC-A or CC-B GS1 composite 2D component is required.

Data syntax: GS1 Application Identifiers.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24724, ITS Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), AIM ISS - Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data field input must be a solitary AI (01) with thirteen or fourteen digits of a GTIN, i.e. (01)....
  • If thirteen digits of AI (01) data are supplied then the check digit is calculated automatically, otherwise the provided check digit will be verified.
  • Deprecated: For internal use. The linkage option signifies the presence of a GS1 composite 2D component.

Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

Data:    (01)09521234543213
Options: 
Encoder: databaromni
Data:    (01)0952123454321
Options: 
Encoder: databaromni

GS1 DataBar Stacked Omnidirectional

GS1 DataBar Stacked Omnidirectional is a fixed-length, stacked linear barcode symbology that can be used to encode a GTIN-14 for use at point of sale.

Also known as: RSS-14 Stacked Omnidirectional.

Uses:

  • Small retail items scanned at point of sale, such as loose fruit and vegetables.

Variants:

  • GS1 DataBar Omnidirectional is a variant of GS1 DataBar Stacked Omnidirectional for use where a shorter, wider symbol is required.
  • GS1 DataBar Stacked Omnidirectional Composite is a variant of GS1 DataBar Stacked Omnidirectional that should be used when a CC-A or CC-B GS1 composite 2D component is required.

Data syntax: GS1 Application Identifiers.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24724, ITS Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), AIM ISS - Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data field input must be a solitary AI (01) with thirteen or fourteen digits of a GTIN, i.e. (01)....
  • If thirteen digits of AI (01) data are supplied then the check digit is calculated automatically, otherwise the provided check digit will be verified.
  • The barxmult option specifies the height of each row in modules, at least 33. The default is 33.
  • Deprecated: For internal use. The linkage option signifies the presence of a GS1 composite 2D component.

Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

Data:    (01)24012345678905
Options: 
Encoder: databarstackedomni
Data:    (01)2401234567890
Options: 
Encoder: databarstackedomni

GS1 DataBar Expanded

GS1 DataBar Expanded is a variable-length, linear barcode symbology that can be used to encode a GTIN-14 alongside a number of other application identifiers for use at point of sale.

Also known as: RSS Expanded.

Uses:

  • Fresh and variable-measure products scanned at point of sale, carrying a weight, price, expiry date or batch with the GTIN.

Variants:

  • GS1 DataBar Expanded Stacked is a variant of GS1 DataBar Expanded for use where a taller, narrower symbol is required.
  • GS1 DataBar Expanded Composite is a variant of GS1 DataBar Expanded that should be used when a CC-A or CC-B GS1 composite 2D component is required.
  • GS1 North American Coupon Code is an application of GS1 DataBar Expanded for manufacturer coupons in the US and Canada.

Data syntax: GS1 Application Identifiers.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24724, ITS Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), AIM ISS - Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data field input is provided in GS1 Application Identifier standard format.
  • Note that it is not necessary to specify FNC1 characters since the encoder will insert these automatically where necessary.
  • Deprecated. The dontlint option disables GS1 Application Identifier syntax validation allowing images to be generated for input that does not comply with GS1 standards.
  • If the data contains a number of application identifiers matching any of the specifications below then they should be provided in this given order for maximum encoding efficiency:
    • (01)9...(3103)... (this and the next four only when no other AIs follow)
    • (01)9...(3202)...
    • (01)9...(3203)...
    • (01)9...(310x/320x)...(11/13/15/17)...
    • (01)9...(310x/320x)...
    • (01)9...(392x)...
    • (01)9...(393x)...
    • (01)...
  • Deprecated: For internal use. The linkage option signifies the presence of a GS1 composite 2D component.

Examples

GTIN 9521234543213; Weight 0.123kg:

Data:    (01)09521234543213(3103)000123
Options:
Encoder: databarexpanded

GS1 DataBar Expanded Stacked

GS1 DataBar Expanded Stacked is a variable-length, stacked-linear barcode symbology that can be used to encode a GTIN-14 alongside a number of other application identifiers for use at point of sale.

Also known as: RSS Expanded Stacked.

Uses:

  • Fresh and variable-measure products scanned at point of sale whose packaging is too narrow for GS1 DataBar Expanded, carrying a weight, price, expiry date or batch with the GTIN.

Variants:

  • GS1 DataBar Expanded is a variant of GS1 DataBar Expanded Stacked for use where a shorter, wider symbol is required.
  • GS1 DataBar Expanded Stacked Composite is a variant of GS1 DataBar Expanded Stacked that should be used when a CC-A or CC-B GS1 composite 2D component is required.
  • GS1 North American Coupon Code is an application of GS1 DataBar Expanded for manufacturer coupons in the US and Canada.

Data syntax: GS1 Application Identifiers.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24724, ITS Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), AIM ISS - Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data field input is provided in GS1 Application Identifier standard format.
  • Note that it is not necessary to specify FNC1 characters since the encoder will insert these automatically where necessary.
  • Deprecated. The dontlint option disables GS1 Application Identifier syntax validation allowing images to be generated for input that does not comply with GS1 standards.
  • If the data contains a number of application identifiers matching any of the specifications below then they should be provided in this given order for maximum encoding efficiency:
    • (01)9...(3103)... (this and the next four only when no other AIs follow)
    • (01)9...(3202)...
    • (01)9...(3203)...
    • (01)9...(310x/320x)...(11/13/15/17)...
    • (01)9...(310x/320x)...
    • (01)9...(392x)...
    • (01)9...(393x)...
    • (01)...
  • The segments option is used to specify the maximum number of segments per row, an even number from 2 to 22. The default is 4.
  • The barxmult option specifies the height of each row in modules, at least 34. The default is 34.
  • Deprecated: For internal use. The linkage option signifies the presence of a GS1 composite 2D component.

Examples

GTIN 9521234543213; Weight 0.123kg:

Data:    (01)09521234543213(3103)000123
Options: segments=4
Encoder: databarexpandedstacked

GS1 DataBar Truncated

GS1 DataBar Truncated is a fixed-length, linear barcode symbology that can be used to encode a GTIN-14 on items not scanned at point of sale.

Also known as: RSS-14 Truncated.

Uses:

  • Small items not scanned at point of sale, such as healthcare products.

Variants:

  • GS1 DataBar Stacked is a variant of GS1 DataBar Truncated for use where a taller, narrower symbol is required.
  • GS1 DataBar Omnidirectional is a variant of GS1 DataBar Truncated of full height for items scanned at point of sale.
  • GS1 DataBar Truncated Composite is a variant of GS1 DataBar Truncated that should be used when a CC-A or CC-B GS1 composite 2D component is required.

Data syntax: GS1 Application Identifiers.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24724, ITS Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), AIM ISS - Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data field input must be a solitary AI (01) with thirteen or fourteen digits of a GTIN, i.e. (01)....
  • If thirteen digits of AI (01) data are supplied then the check digit is calculated automatically, otherwise the provided check digit will be verified.
  • Deprecated: For internal use. The linkage option signifies the presence of a GS1 composite 2D component.

Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

Data:    (01)09521234543213
Options: 
Encoder: databartruncated
Data:    (01)0952123454321
Options: 
Encoder: databartruncated

GS1 DataBar Stacked

GS1 DataBar Stacked is a fixed-length, stacked linear barcode symbology that can be used to encode a GTIN-14 on items not scanned at point of sale.

Also known as: RSS-14 Stacked.

Uses:

  • Small items not scanned at point of sale, such as healthcare products.

Variants:

  • GS1 DataBar Truncated is a variant of GS1 DataBar Stacked for use where a shorter, wider symbol is required.
  • GS1 DataBar Stacked Composite is a variant of GS1 DataBar Stacked that should be used when a CC-A or CC-B GS1 composite 2D component is required.

Data syntax: GS1 Application Identifiers.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24724, ITS Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), AIM ISS - Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data field input must be a solitary AI (01) with thirteen or fourteen digits of a GTIN, i.e. (01)....
  • If thirteen digits of AI (01) data are supplied then the check digit is calculated automatically, otherwise the provided check digit will be verified.
  • Deprecated: For internal use. The linkage option signifies the presence of a GS1 composite 2D component.

Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

Data:    (01)09521234543213
Options: 
Encoder: databarstacked
Data:    (01)0952123454321
Options: 
Encoder: databarstacked

GS1 DataBar Limited

GS1 DataBar Limited is a fixed-length, linear barcode symbology that can be used to encode a GTIN-14 beginning with 0 or 1 on items not scanned at point of sale.

Also known as: RSS Limited.

Uses:

  • Small items not scanned at point of sale, such as healthcare products.

Variants:

  • GS1 DataBar Limited Composite is a variant of GS1 DataBar Limited that should be used when a CC-A or CC-B GS1 composite 2D component is required.

Data syntax: GS1 Application Identifiers.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24724, ITS Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), AIM ISS - Reduced Space Symbology (RSS), GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data field input must be a solitary AI (01) with thirteen or fourteen digits of a GTIN starting with 0 or 1, i.e. (01)0... or (01)1....
  • If thirteen digits of AI (01) data are supplied then the check digit is calculated automatically, otherwise the provided check digit will be verified.
  • Deprecated: For internal use. The linkage option signifies the presence of a GS1 composite 2D component.

Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

Data:    (01)09521234543213
Options: 
Encoder: databarlimited
Data:    (01)0952123454321
Options: 
Encoder: databarlimited

GS1 North American Coupon Code

GS1 North American Coupon Code is an implementation of the GS1 DataBar Expanded barcode symbology with AI (8110) that is used for paper manufacturer coupons at point of sale.

Also known as: GS1 DataBar Coupon, U.S. Coupon Code.

Uses:

  • Manufacturer coupons redeemed at point of sale in the US and Canada, which replaced the UPC prefix 5 coupons.

Data syntax: GS1 Application Identifiers.

Standards: North American Coupon Application Guideline Using GS1 DataBar Expanded Symbols, ISO/IEC 24724, GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data field input is provided in GS1 Application Identifier standard format and must be a solitary AI (8110).
  • The includetext option shows the GS1 Company Prefix and Offer Code, separated by a dash, above the symbol.
  • The segments option is used to specify the maximum number of segments per row which must be an even number. The default is 4.
  • The following options control the placement and styling of the coupon text above the symbol. Each is equivalent to the corresponding text1* option (see Text Properties):
    • coupontext: Override the coupon label content
    • coupontextfont: PostScript font name for text above symbol
    • coupontextsize: Font size for the text above symbol, in points
    • coupontextcolor: Colour for the text above symbol
    • coupontextxalign, coupontextyalign: Alignment of the text above symbol
    • coupontextxoffset, coupontextyoffset: Position of the text above symbol, in points
    • coupontextdirection: Direction of the text above symbol
    • coupontextgaps: Gap between characters in the text above symbol, in points
    • coupontextsubspace, coupontextsplit, coupontextlinegaps: Multi-line text formatting

Examples

A coupon code with eight segments per row:

Data:    (8110)106141416543213500110000310123196000
Options: includetext segments=8
Encoder: gs1northamericancoupon

The coupon label can be styled using the coupontext* options (or the equivalent text1*):

Data:    (8110)106141416543213500110000310123196000
Options: includetext segments=8 coupontextcolor=FF0000 coupontextxalign=center
Encoder: gs1northamericancoupon

Postal Symbols

Australia Post 4 State Customer Code

The Australia Post 4 State Customer Code is a barcode used by Australia Post to encode the data on letter mail.

Also known as: 4SCC, 4 State Customer Code.

Uses:

  • Letter mail in Australia, carrying the Delivery Point Identifier (DPID) for automated sorting.

Standards: Australia Post Customer Barcode Technical Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The first two digits of the data field are the mandatory Format Control Code (FCC), either:
    • 11: Customer Barcode 1 ("Standard Customer Barcode")
    • 45: Reply Paid Barcode
    • 59: Customer Barcode 2
    • 62: Customer Barcode 3
    • 87: Routing Barcode
    • 92: Redirection Barcode
  • The next eight characters are digits that specify the mandatory DPID.
  • Any remaining characters specify the customer information field, which FCCs 11, 45, 87 and 92 do not have. FCC 59 takes up to 8 digits or 5 characters, and FCC 62 up to 15 digits or 10 characters, in one of two alphabets:
    • The custinfoenc option should be supplied as custinfoenc=numeric if the customer information field is to be encoded using the numeric alphabet which can contain the digits 0-9.
    • Otherwise the customer information field is encoded using the default character encoding, custinfoenc=character, which permits any of the following characters:
      • Upper case letters A-Z
      • Lower case letters a-z
      • Digits 0-9
      • Symbols space and #

Examples

FCC 62 symbol with character customer data:

Data:    6279438541AaaB 155
Options: custinfoenc=character includetext
Encoder: auspost

FCC 59 symbol with numeric customer data:

Data:    593221132401234567
Options: custinfoenc=numeric includetext
Encoder: auspost

Canada Post PostBar

Canada Post PostBar is the family of 4-state barcodes of Canada Post that is disclosed in US Patent 5,602,382, each with a Data Content Identifier (DCI) giving its structure and Reed-Solomon error correction over GF(64).

Uses:

  • Sortation and tracking of mail by Canada Post.

Standards: US Patent 5,602,382 - Mail piece bar code having a data content identifier; Canada Post 4-State Bar Code Handbook (bar dimensions).

Data and Options

  • The data field is the DCI followed by the fields of the format, which is selected by the length of the data:
    • PostBar.C10 (11 characters, 56 bars), applied by Canada Post's machines: a DCI from V to Z, the six-character postal code, and the four bars of the machine ID as digits from 0 (full bar) to 3 (tracker).
    • PostBar.G12 (12 characters, 49 bars), for international mail: a DCI from 1 to 9, the three-digit country code, and an eight-character postal code padded with spaces.
    • PostBar.S21 (21 characters, 79 bars), for customer services: a DCI from M to U, the bar code sequencer, 0 for a single symbol or 1 or 2 for the first or second of two, and 19 characters of service information.
    • PostBar.D22 (22 characters, 79 bars), applied by customers to domestic mail: a DCI from A to L, the six-character postal code, a four-character address locator and eleven characters of customer information.
  • Postal codes are written without a space, alternating letters and digits. The other fields contain spaces, upper case letters and digits.
  • The structures of Canada Post's Postal Encoding Module, such as D52.01 and D82.02, are not available, since their encodation is not published.

Examples

A domestic bar code, PostBar.D22:

Data:    CH0H0H01420NOTEPAPER01
Options:
Encoder: postbar

An international bar code, PostBar.G12:

Data:    9826AB12 3CD
Options:
Encoder: postbar

CEPNet

The CEPNet barcode symbology is used by Correios, the Brazilian postal service, to encode the CEP postal code on letter mail. It has the bars of USPS POSTNET.

Uses:

  • Brazilian mail.

Standards: Correios Guia Técnico - CEPNet e Código 2D para Triagem e Endereçamento.

Data and Options

  • The data field contains the eight digits of the CEP, without a dash.
  • The mandatory check digit is calculated automatically, unless validatecheck is given.
  • The validatecheck option takes the last digit of the data to be the check digit and refuses the data if it is wrong.
  • The includecheckintext option makes the check digit appear in the human readable text.
  • The guide gives bars from 0.015 to 0.025 inches wide at 22 +/- 2 bars per inch, with tall bars from 0.115 to 0.135 inches high. The encoder's defaults are the midpoints, bars 0.020 inches wide and 0.125 inches high.

Examples

Data:    01234567
Options: includetext
Encoder: cepnet

DPD Parcel Label

The DPD Parcel Label barcode is a Code 128 barcode on the parcel labels of the DPD (Geopost) parcel carriers that carries the destination postal code, the tracking number, the service code and the destination country.

Uses:

  • Routing and tracking of parcels by the DPD group.

Standards: Geopost Barcode & Label Layout Specification (GeoLabel); DPD Parcel Label Specification, whose section 6.1.2 describes the relabel.

Data and Options

  • The data field is the 27 characters that follow the identification tag, optionally preceded by the tag. The tag is % unless it is given:
    • The destination postal code, seven characters padded on the left with zeros.
    • The tracking number, a four-digit range code and a ten-digit parcel number, the first two characters of which may be letters.
    • The three-digit service code.
    • The three-digit destination country or network code.
  • The postal code and the first two characters of the tracking number may be upper case letters or digits. The remaining characters are digits.
  • The human readable text is the data in groups, followed by its ISO/IEC 7064 MOD 37,36 check character, which is not encoded in the barcode.
  • The relabel option creates the barcode of a relabel, which has no identification tag and half the height.
  • The default height is one inch, or half an inch for a relabel. The X-dimension of the specification is from 0.375mm to 0.5mm, or to 0.4mm for thermal printing, and the height 25mm, or 12.5mm for a relabel.

Examples

Data:    005432155550001234567101826
Options: includetext
Encoder: dpd

A relabel:

Data:    009876555550007654321136276
Options: includetext relabel
Encoder: dpd

Deutsche Post Identcode

Deutsche Post Identcode is an implementation of the Interleaved 2 of 5 barcode symbology that is used by Deutsche Post to identify parcels for tracking.

Also known as: DHL Identcode.

Uses:

  • Deutsche Post (DHL) parcels: the parcel's identification for tracking.

Standards: Deutsche Post AG Identcode.

Data and Options

  • The data consists of a consecutive string of eleven or twelve digits consisting of:
    • Two-digit primary distribution centre identifier
    • Three-digit customer identifier
    • Six-digit mail piece identifier
    • One-digit check digit (may be omitted)
  • If eleven digits are supplied then the check digit is calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided check digit will be verified.

Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

Data:    563102430313
Options: includetext
Encoder: identcode
Data:    56310243031
Options: includetext
Encoder: identcode

Deutsche Post Leitcode

Deutsche Post Leitcode is an implementation of the Interleaved 2 of 5 barcode symbology that is used by Deutsche Post for mail routing.

Also known as: DHL Leitcode.

Uses:

  • Deutsche Post (DHL) parcels: the destination's routing code (postcode, street and house number).

Standards: Deutsche Post AG Leitcode.

Data and Options

  • The data consists of a consecutive string of thirteen or fourteen digits consisting of:
    • Five-digit postal code
    • Three-digit street identifier
    • Three-digit house number
    • Two-digit product code
    • One-digit check digit (may be omitted)
  • If thirteen digits are supplied then the check digit is calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided check digit will be verified.

Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

Data:    21348075016401
Options: includetext
Encoder: leitcode
Data:    2134807501640
Options: includetext
Encoder: leitcode

Japan Post 4 State Barcode

The Japan Post 4 state barcode symbology is used by the Japan Post service to encode the delivery point identifier on letter mail.

Also known as: Kasutama Barcode, Customer Barcode.

Uses:

  • Mail in Japan: the customer barcode, carrying the postcode and address.

Standards: Japan Post Customer Barcode Technical Specification.

Data and Options

  • The data may contain any of the following characters:
    • Capital letters A-Z
    • Digits 0-9
    • Hyphen -
  • The data is at most 20 characters, each letter counting as two.
  • The mandatory check digit is calculated automatically.
  • The includecheckintext option makes the calculated check digit appear in the human readable text.

Examples

A delivery point identifier:

Data:    6540123789-A-K-Z
Options:
Encoder: japanpost

Korea Post

The Korea Post customer barcode encodes a six-digit Korean postcode and a check digit for the automatic sorting of letter mail. Each digit is five equally spaced positions holding three bars, followed by a bar that separates it from the next, and the digits are printed from the least significant.

Korea Post replaced the six-digit postcodes with five-digit postcodes in August 2015.

Uses:

  • Korean bulk mail, printed by the sender.

Standards: Korea Post customer barcode, as described by ETRI (Electronics and Telecommunications Trends, 1999).

Data and Options

  • The data field contains the six digits of the postcode.
  • The mandatory check digit is calculated automatically, unless validatecheck is given.
  • The validatecheck option takes the last digit of the data to be the check digit and refuses the data if it is wrong.
  • The includecheckintext option makes the check digit appear in the human readable text.

Examples

Data:    123456
Options: includetext
Encoder: koreapost

MaxiCode

The MaxiCode barcode symbology is a 2D barcode based on a hexagonal matrix surrounding a bulls eye pattern. It can encode a structured carrier message and full 256 character extended-ASCII.

Also known as: UPS Code, Code 6, Dense Code.

Uses:

  • UPS parcel labels, carrying the structured carrier message (postcode, country and service class).

Variants:

  • UPS MaxiCode is a variant of MaxiCode that validates the UPS message of a package label.

Standards: ISO/IEC 16023, ANSI/AIM BC10 - ISS MaxiCode.

Data and Options

  • The mode option is used to specify how the data is structured in the symbol:
    • mode=2 - Formatted data containing a Structured Carrier Message with a numeric (US domestic) postal code.
    • mode=3 - Formatted data containing a Structured Carrier Message with an alphanumeric (international) postal code.
    • mode=4 - Unstructured extended ASCII data using standard error correction.
    • mode=5 - Unstructured extended ASCII data using enhanced error correction.
    • mode=6 - Barcode reader programming.
  • If mode is unspecified the encoder will default to selecting mode=5 if the encoded length of the input data permits enhanced error correction, otherwise it will select mode=4 which provides standard error correction.
  • The default interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1. When supported by the receiver characters from other code pages can be encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • When the parsefnc option is specified, non-data function characters can be specified by escape sequences:
    • ^ECI000000 to ^ECI999999: ECI indicators
  • If mode=4, mode=5 or mode=6 the data field may contain any extended ASCII data.
  • If mode=2 or mode=3 the data field must begin with a properly structured carrier message, followed by any extended ASCII data.
  • The structured carrier message contains a postal code, a three-digit ISO country code and a three-digit class of service separated by GS (ASCII 29) characters. It is formatted in the data field as follows: [postal code]^029[country code]^029[service class]^029. If mode=2 the postcode is up to nine digits, whilst if mode=3 the postcode is up to six characters from capital letters, digits, space and "#$%&'()*+,-./:.
  • Alternatively, messages may begin with the special application field identifier "[)>{RS}01{GS}yy" where "{RS}" represents ASCII value 30, "{GS}" represents ASCII value 29 and "yy" is a two-digit year. In parse mode this is represented as [)>^03001^029yy. If mode=2 or mode=3 this must be immediately followed by the structured carrier message.
  • The sam option specifies this symbol to be part of multi-part structured data held in up to eight symbols. For example sam=25 specifies this to be the second symbol in a group of five symbols.
  • The sampos and samtotal options are an alternative to sam that give the position and the total separately, for example sampos=2 samtotal=5. They cannot be combined with sam.

Rendering

  • Dark hexagons are drawn 0.12mm narrower than the module pitch, as the specification requires, and inkspread reduces them further, so inkspread=0 gives the nominal dimensions.
  • MaxiCode is a fixed-size symbology so strictspec bounds the X-dimension to the permitted symbol width of 24mm to 27mm.
  • Bitmap output should use gridfit, which follows the practical printing guidance of ISO/IEC 16023 Annex J: whole device pixels per module and, at resolutions below about 850 DPI, pixel fonts for the hexagons and finder pattern.

Examples

Identical symbols encoding unstructured data, the latter using the parse option:

Data:    This is MaxiCode
Options:
Encoder: maxicode
Data:    This is Maxi^067ode
Options: parse
Encoder: maxicode

A mode 2 symbol with a numeric postal code:

Data:    152382802^029840^029001^0291Z00004951^029UPSN^02906X610\
         ^029159^0291234567^0291/1^029^029Y\
         ^029634 ALPHA DR^029PITTSBURGH^029PA^029^004
Options: mode=2 parse
Encoder: maxicode

A mode 3 symbol with an alphanumeric postal code:

Data:    ABC123^029840^029001^0291Z00004951^029UPSN^02906X610\
         ^029159^0291234567^0291/1^029^029Y\
         ^029634 ALPHA DR^029PITTSBURGH^029PA^029^004
Options: mode=3 parse
Encoder: maxicode

A mode 2 symbol with an application field identifier:

Data:    [)>^03001^02996152382802^029840^029001^0291Z00004951\
         ^029UPSN^02906X610^029159^0291234567^0291/1^029^029Y\
         ^029634 ALPHA DR^029PITTSBURGH^029PA^029^004
Options: mode=2 parse
Encoder: maxicode

UPS MaxiCode

UPS MaxiCode is the use of MaxiCode on UPS package labels, carrying a structured carrier message with the destination postal code, country and class of service, followed by the UPS shipment details.

Standards: ISO/IEC 16023 MaxiCode; UPS Guide to Bar Coding, which is available to UPS customers.

Data and Options

  • The data field is the message of 14 fields separated by GS characters, optionally enclosed by the header [)>{RS}01{GS}yy, where yy is the two digit format version, and the trailer {RS}{EOT}:
    • The ship to postal code, of five or nine digits, or up to six upper case letters, digits or spaces.
    • The three digit ship to country code.
    • The three digit class of service.
    • The tracking number, ten upper case letters or digits.
    • The carrier code, UPSN.
    • The shipper number, six upper case letters or digits.
    • The three digit day of the year of pickup.
    • The shipment ID, of up to 30 characters, which may be empty.
    • The package of packages, as n/x.
    • The weight in pounds, of up to three digits, which may be empty.
    • The address validation flag, Y or N.
    • The ship to address, of up to 35 characters, which may be empty.
    • The ship to city, of up to 20 characters.
    • The ship to state, two upper case letters.
  • The symbol is in mode 2 for a postal code of five or nine digits, otherwise in mode 3.
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying GS as ^029, RS as ^030 and EOT as ^004.

Examples

Data:    [)>^030\
         01^02996\
         123450001^029\
         840^029\
         001^029\
         1Z12345678^029\
         UPSN^029\
         A1B2C3^029\
         042^029\
         8901234^029\
         1/2^029\
         5^029\
         Y^029\
         12 EXAMPLE ST^029\
         SPRINGTON^029\
         CA^030^004
Options: parse
Encoder: upsmaxicode

Royal Mail 4 State Customer Code

The Royal Mail 4 State Customer Code is a barcode symbology used by Royal Mail to encode the postcode and delivery point identifier on letter mail.

Also known as: RM4SCC, CBC, BPO 4 State Code.

Uses:

  • UK business mail sorted by postcode and delivery point, now largely replaced by Mailmark.

Standards: BS 14500.

Data and Options

  • The data may contain any of the following characters from the postcode and DPID:
    • Capital letters A-Z
    • Digits 0-9
  • The mandatory check character is calculated automatically, unless validatecheck is given.
  • The validatecheck option takes the last character of the data to be the check character and refuses the data if it is wrong.
  • The includecheckintext option makes the check character appear in the human readable text.

Examples

A postcode and delivery point identifier:

Data:    LE28HS9Z
Options: includetext
Encoder: royalmail

Mailmark

Royal Mail Mailmark is an implementation of the Data Matrix (ECC 200) barcode symbology for application within the Royal Mail postal system.

Uses:

  • UK mail sorted and tracked by Royal Mail.

Variants:

  • Royal Mail Mailmark 4-state is the 4-state barcode form of Mailmark, for mailers that cannot print Data Matrix.

Standards: Royal Mail Mailmark Barcode Definition Document.

Data and Options

  • The data field input consists of 45 characters of Mailmark structured data (including required space padding) followed by variable-length, free-formatted customer data.
  • Note: Due to the fixed-length field format of the message data it is important to carefully preserve spaces in the data field.
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • The mandatory type option is used to specify the size of the symbol, either 7 (24x24), 9 (32x32) or 29 (16x48).

Examples

A type 29 (16x48) symbol:

Data:    JGB 012100123412345678AB19XY1A 0             www.xyz.com
Options: type=29
Encoder: mailmark

Mailmark 4-state

Royal Mail Mailmark 4-state is a 4-state barcode for application within the Royal Mail postal system, for mailers that cannot print the Data Matrix form of Mailmark. It carries the mailing's identifiers and destination postcode with Reed-Solomon error correction.

Uses:

  • UK machine-readable Low Sort and Unsorted letters sorted and tracked by Royal Mail.
  • Manual Mailmark parcels and general large letters.

Standards: Royal Mail Mailmark Barcode Definition Document; Royal Mail Mailmark barcode C and barcode L encoding and decoding instructions.

Data and Options

  • The data field consists of the fixed-length Mailmark fields, including any space padding: 22 characters for barcode C (66 bars) or 26 characters for barcode L (78 bars):
    • Format, 0 to 4.
    • Version ID, 1.
    • Class, 0 to 9 or A to E.
    • Supply Chain ID, two digits for barcode C or six for barcode L.
    • Item ID, eight digits.
    • Destination Post Code plus Delivery Point Suffix, nine characters: a full postcode followed by its two-character Delivery Point Suffix, padded with spaces at the end, or XY11 followed by five spaces for an international destination.
  • Note: Due to the fixed-length field format of the data it is important to carefully preserve spaces in the data field.

Examples

A barcode C:

Data:    1101234567890ZZ999ZZ1A
Options:
Encoder: mailmark4state

A barcode L:

Data:    41012345678901234ZZ999ZZ1A
Options:
Encoder: mailmark4state

Royal TNT Post 4 state barcode

The Royal TNT Post 4 state barcode symbology is used by PostNL to encode the delivery point identifier on letter mail.

Also known as: KIX, Klant IndeX.

Uses:

  • Mail in the Netherlands (PostNL), carrying the postcode and house number.

Standards: TPG Post Kix Code Specification.

Data and Options

  • The data may contain:
    • Capital letters A-Z
    • Digits 0-9

Examples

A delivery point identifier:

Data:    1231FZ13XHS
Options: includetext
Encoder: kix

UPU S10

UPU S10 is a Code 128 barcode carrying the 13-character S10 identifier of the Universal Postal Union, which identifies postal items, such as registered mail and parcels, as they pass between postal operators.

Uses:

  • International tracked postal items.
  • Domestic postal items of many postal operators.

Standards: UPU S10 - Identification of postal items - 13-character identifier.

Data and Options

  • The data field is the S10 identifier: a two-letter service indicator, an eight-digit serial number, a check digit and the two-letter ISO country code of the issuing postal operator, without spaces.
  • If the check digit is omitted then the encoder will calculate and add it. If it is given then it is verified.
  • Service indicators beginning with J, K, S, T or W are reserved and are refused.
  • The human readable text is spaced in groups for readability.
  • The default height is half an inch. The X-dimension of the standard is from 0.25mm to 0.51mm, with a minimum of 0.33mm recommended. The height is at least 9mm and 15% of the width of the symbol, with a minimum of 12.5mm recommended.

Examples

Data:    EE471108151FR
Options: includetext
Encoder: upus10

With the check digit calculated:

Data:    RR47312482GB
Options: includetext
Encoder: upus10

USPS Intelligent Mail

The USPS Intelligent Mail barcode is used by the US Postal Service to encode the delivery and sender information on letter mail.

Also known as: USPS OneCode.

Uses:

  • US letters and flats, for automation prices and tracking.

Standards: USPS-B-3200.

Data and Options

  • The data contains 20, 25, 29 or 31 digits representing the following:
    • Barcode Identifier - two digits
    • Service Type Identifier - three digits
    • Mailer ID, Sequence Number - either six then nine digits respectively or nine then six digits respectively
    • Delivery Point ZIP Code - none, five, nine or eleven digits
  • An 11-bit CRC is added automatically.

Examples

A 31-digit mail tracking barcode:

Data:    0123456709498765432101234567891
Options: includetext
Encoder: onecode

USPS POSTNET

The USPS POSTNET barcode symbology is used by the US Postal Service to encode the ZIP code information on letter mail.

Uses:

  • US mail, superseded by the USPS Intelligent Mail barcode.

Variants:

  • CEPNet has the bars of POSTNET and carries the Brazilian CEP postal code.

Standards: USPS Publication 25.

Data and Options

  • The data field contains five, nine or eleven digits (ZIP, ZIP+4, or ZIP+4 and delivery point), without dashes.
  • The mandatory check digit is calculated automatically, unless validatecheck is given.
  • The validatecheck option takes the last digit of the data to be the check digit and refuses the data if it is wrong.
  • The includecheckintext option makes the check digit appear in the human readable text.

Examples

A ZIP+4+delivery point code:

Data:    12345123412
Options:
Encoder: postnet

USPS PLANET

The USPS PLANET barcode symbology is used by the US Postal Service to track letter mail.

Uses:

  • US mail, superseded by the USPS Intelligent Mail barcode.

Standards: USPS Publication 25.

Data and Options

  • The data field contains eleven or thirteen digits, without dashes.
  • The mandatory check digit is calculated automatically, unless validatecheck is given.
  • The validatecheck option takes the last digit of the data to be the check digit and refuses the data if it is wrong.
  • The includecheckintext option makes the check digit appear in the human readable text.

Examples

An 11-digit PLANET code:

Data:    01234567890
Options:
Encoder: planet

USPS FIM Symbols

The symbol encoder generates the USPS Facing Identification Marks.

Uses:

  • Facing identification marks on US business reply and courtesy reply mail.

Standards: USPS Publication 25.

Data and Options

  • The data field accepts one of the following values:
    • fima - FIM-A
    • fimb - FIM-B
    • fimc - FIM-C
    • fimd - FIM-D
    • fime - FIM-E

Examples

A USPS FIM A symbol:

Data:    fima
Options: 
Encoder: symbol

A USPS FIM B symbol:

Data:    fimb
Options: 
Encoder: symbol

A USPS FIM C symbol:

Data:    fimc
Options: 
Encoder: symbol

A USPS FIM D symbol:

Data:    fimd
Options: 
Encoder: symbol

Pharmaceutical Symbols

Italian Pharmacode

Italian Pharmacode is an implementation of the Code 39 barcode symbology that is used for pharmaceutical products in Italy.

Also known as: Code 32, IMH, Radix 32.

Uses:

  • Medicines in Italy: the Codice Farmaceutico (AIC) on packs.

Standards: Italian Ministerial Decree 2003.

Data and Options

  • The data field must contain either eight or nine digits from the code. The leading A which is provided in some applications must be omitted; it is added to the human readable text.
  • The mandatory check digit is calculated automatically if it is not provided, otherwise the provided check digit is verified.

Examples

Identical symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

Data:    012345676
Options: includetext
Encoder: code32
Data:    01234567
Options: includetext
Encoder: code32

Pharmacode

Pharmacode is a binary barcode symbology that is used by the pharmaceutical industry.

Also known as: Pharmaceutical Binary Code, Laetus Code.

Uses:

  • Checking the printed packaging materials of pharmaceuticals on packaging lines, rather than identifying an item in trade.

Variants:

  • Two-track Pharmacode is a variant of the Pharmacode barcode.

Data and Options

  • The data field must contain a number between 3 and 131070 inclusive.
  • The nwidth, wwidth and swidth options can be used to specify a custom width, in modules, for the narrow bars, wide bars and inter-bar spaces respectively. The defaults are 1, 3 and 2.

Examples

A basic symbol:

Data:    117480
Options:
Encoder: pharmacode

A symbol with custom bar widths:

Data:    117480
Options: nwidth=2 wwidth=6 swidth=4
Encoder: pharmacode

Two-Track Pharmacode

Two-Track Pharmacode is a binary barcode symbology used by the pharmaceutical industry.

Also known as: Two-track Pharmaceutical Binary Code, Two-track Laetus Code.

Uses:

  • Checking the printed packaging materials of pharmaceuticals on packaging lines, rather than identifying an item in trade.

Variants:

  • Pharmacode is the one-track form.

Data and Options

  • The data field must contain a number between 4 and 64570080 inclusive.
  • The height option specifies the height of each of the two tracks in inches, so a full-height bar is twice as tall. The default is 4mm (height=0.1575).

Examples

A basic symbol:

Data:    117480
Options:
Encoder: pharmacode2

PZN

PZN is a discrete, fixed length, self-checking barcode symbology used for pharmaceutical products in Germany.

Also known as: Pharmazentralnummer.

Uses:

  • Medicines in Germany: the Pharmazentralnummer (PZN) on packs.

Variants:

  • PZN7 is the seven-digit format.
  • PZN8 is the eight-digit format.

Standards: IFA Coding System PZN.

Data and Options

  • For the default PZN7 encoding, the data field must contain six digits or seven digits.
  • The pzn8 option specifies that a PZN8 symbol is required, in which case the data field must contain seven digits or eight digits.
  • The mandatory check digit is calculated automatically if not provided, otherwise the provided check digit is verified.
  • A number whose check value is 10 has no valid check digit and cannot be encoded.

Examples

Identical PZN7 symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

Data:    1234562
Options: includetext
Encoder: pzn
Data:    123456
Options: includetext
Encoder: pzn

Identical PZN8 symbols, input provided with and without a check digit:

Data:    0275808
Options: pzn8 includetext
Encoder: pzn
Data:    02758089
Options: pzn8 includetext
Encoder: pzn

PPN-Code

The PPN-Code is a Data Matrix symbol on the packs of pharmaceutical products that carries the Pharmacy Product Number (PPN), with the serial number, batch number and expiry date used to verify the pack, as data elements with ASC MH10 Data Identifiers in the ISO/IEC 15434 Format 06 envelope.

Uses:

  • Packs of pharmaceutical products in Germany and other markets whose numbering agencies have a PRA Code, including verification under the EU Falsified Medicines Directive (securPharm).

Standards: IFA PPN-Code Specification for Retail Packaging; ISO/IEC 15434; ISO/IEC 15418; ISO/IEC 16022.

Data and Options

  • The data field contains the data elements, each a Data Identifier followed by its data, separated by GS characters. The envelope is added by the encoder.
  • The elements are in any order, and those of the specification are validated:
    • 9N - The Pharmacy Product Number, which is required: a PRA Code, the product number and two check digits. For PRA Code 11 the product number is a German PZN, whose check digit is also verified.
    • S - The serial number, up to 20 characters of the GS1 character set 82.
    • 1T - The batch number, up to 20 characters of the GS1 character set 82.
    • D - The expiry date, as YYMMDD, with day 00 for the month alone.
    • 8P - An additional GTIN or NTIN, which may be repeated.
  • Other Data Identifiers may be included.
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying the GS separators as ^029.
  • The options of Data Matrix are available, such as format=rectangle or dmre for a rectangular symbol.
  • The X-dimension of the specification is from 0.25mm to 0.99mm, typically 0.35mm.

Examples

Data:    9N112048163909^029\
         1TBATCH42^029\
         D281200^029\
         SA1B2C3D4E5
Options: parse
Encoder: ppncode

HIBC Symbols

HIBC barcodes use a number of general symbologies as carrier symbols for data structured according to the LIC and PAS structured data definitions.

Uses:

  • Healthcare products and medical devices labelled to the Health Industry Bar Code (HIBC) standards, including the UDI of devices issued through HIBCC.

Variants:

  • HIBC Code 39 is a variant of Code 39.
  • HIBC Code 128 is a variant of Code 128.
  • HIBC PDF417 is a variant of PDF417.
  • HIBC MicroPDF417 is a variant of MicroPDF417.
  • HIBC QR Code is a variant of QR Code.
  • HIBC Data Matrix is a variant of Data Matrix.
  • HIBC Data Matrix Rectangular is a variant of Data Matrix Rectangular.
  • HIBC Codablock F is a variant of Codablock F.
  • HIBC Aztec Code is a variant of Aztec Code.

Data syntax: HIBC LIC/PAS.

Standards: ANSI/HIBC Provider Applications Standard, ANSI/HIBC Supplier Labelling Standard, ANSI/HIBC Positive Identification for Patient Safety, ANSI/HIBC Syntax Standard.

Data and Options

  • The data is the HIBC LIC or PAS data, without the leading +, and contains only digits, capital letters, space and -.$/+%.
  • The HIBC + character is prefixed automatically.
  • The mandatory HIBC check character is automatically appended to the input, unless validatecheck is given.
  • The validatecheck option takes the last character of the data to be the check character and refuses the data if it is wrong.

HIBC Code 39

Data:    A999BJC5D6E71
Options: includetext
Encoder: hibccode39

HIBC Code 128

Data:    A999BJC5D6E71
Options: includetext
Encoder: hibccode128

Data:    A999BJC5D6E71
Options: 
Encoder: hibcpdf417

Data:    A999BJC5D6E71
Options: 
Encoder: hibcmicropdf417

Data:    A999BJC5D6E71
Options:
Encoder: hibcqrcode

HIBC Data Matrix

Data:    A999BJC5D6E71
Options:
Encoder: hibcdatamatrix

Data:    A999BJC5D6E71
Options:
Encoder: hibcdatamatrixrectangular

Data:    A999BJC5D6E71

Options:
