Less-used Symbols

BC412

The BC412 barcode symbology is a single-width, variable-length barcode that is used for silicon wafer identification by the semiconductor manufacturing industry.

Also known as: BC412 SEMI, BC412 IBM.

Uses:

  • Silicon wafer identification in semiconductor fabs (SEMI T1).

Standards: SEMI T1.

Data and Options

  • The data field can hold any of the following:
    • Numbers 0-9
    • Capital letters A-Z, excluding O
  • The includestartstop option adds start and stop bars.
  • The includecheck option calculates the check character.
  • The validatecheck option takes the last character of the data (the second with semi) to be the check character and refuses the data if it is wrong.
  • The includecheckintext option makes the calculated check character appear in the human readable text.
  • The semi option enables conformance to the SEMI standard by enabling start and stop bars and a check character, which is placed in the second position rather than appended. The data must be 7 to 18 characters.
  • The inkspread option can be used to adjust the width of the bars.

Examples

A symbol with a check character:

Data:    BC412
Options: includecheck
Encoder: bc412

A symbol with start and stop bars:

Data:    BC412
Options: includestartstop
Encoder: bc412

A SEMI-compliant symbol:

Data:    BC412SEMIEXAMPLE
Options: semi
Encoder: bc412

Channel Code

Channel Code is a linear, continuous, self-checking, bidirectional barcode symbology that encodes between two and seven digits in a short space.

Standards: ANSI/AIM BC12 - USS Channel Code.

Data and Options

  • The data field can hold zero prefixed values from any of the following ranges:
    • Channel 3: 00-26
    • Channel 4: 000-292
    • Channel 5: 0000-3493
    • Channel 6: 00000-44072
    • Channel 7: 000000-576688
    • Channel 8: 0000000-7742862
  • The channel is determined to be one more than the number of digits given in the data field.
  • The shortfinder option generates a symbol with a shortened finder pattern.
  • The includecheck option appends an optional check bar suffix.

Examples

A channel 3 symbol holding the value five:

Data:    05
Options: includetext
Encoder: channelcode

A channel 4 symbol holding the value 123:

Data:    123
Options: includetext
Encoder: channelcode

A channel 4 symbol holding the value five including optional check bars:

Data:    005
Options: includetext includecheck
Encoder: channelcode

A channel 3 symbol holding the value 26 with a shortened finder pattern:

Data:    26
Options: shortfinder includetext
Encoder: channelcode

Codabar

Codabar is a linear, discrete, self-checking, bidirectional barcode symbology that can encode digits, six symbols and four delimiter characters.

Also known as: Rationalized Codabar, Ames Code, NW-7, USD-4, USS-Codabar, ABC Codabar, Monarch, Code 2 of 7.

Uses:

  • Library books and library cards.

Standards: ANSI/AIM BC3 - USS Codabar, BS EN 798.

Data and Options

  • The data field must start and stop with one of the following delimiters
    • ABCD
    • TNE* (with the altstartstop option)
  • The data field can otherwise hold any of the following
    • Digits 0-9
    • Symbols -$:/.+
  • The altstartstop option specifies that the alternative set of delimiter characters is in use.
  • The includecheck option calculates the check character.
  • The validatecheck option takes the last character before the stop delimiter to be the check character and refuses the data if it is wrong.
  • The includecheckintext option makes the calculated check character appear in the human readable text.

Examples

A symbol with a check digit:

Data:    A0123456789B
Options: includecheck includetext includecheckintext
Encoder: rationalizedCodabar

A symbol with alternative start/stop delimiters:

Data:    T0123456789N
Options: altstartstop includetext
Encoder: rationalizedCodabar

Codablock F

The Codablock F barcode symbology is a 2D stacked-linear barcode that consists of a number of stacked Code 128 symbols. It can encode full 256 character extended-ASCII.

Variants:

  • HIBC Codablock F is a variant of Codablock F that should be used when encoding HIBC formatted data.
  • Codablock A is the related symbology whose rows are Code 39 symbols.

Standards: USS Codablock F.

Data and Options

  • The data field can consist of any extended-ASCII data. The default interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
  • FNC4 function characters will be inserted automatically to allow the encoding of extended ASCII characters.
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • When the parsefnc option is specified, non-data function characters can be specified by escape sequences:
    • ^FNC1: FNC1
    • ^FNC3: FNC3
  • The columns option specifies the number of columns in the symbol, from 4 to 62, default 8.
  • The rows option specifies the number of rows in the symbol, between 2 and 44.
  • If rows is unspecified the encoder will default to the smallest number of rows that can hold the given data.
  • The rowheight option specifies the height of the bars in each row in modules, from 8 to 50. The default is 10.
  • The sepheight option specifies the height of the separator bars enclosing the rows in modules, from 1 to 5. The default is 1.

Examples

A basic symbol:

Data:    Codablock F
Options:
Encoder: codablockf

A symbol with fixed dimensions:

Data:    CODABLOCK F 34567890123456789010040digit
Options: columns=8 rows=5
Encoder: codablockf

A symbol with custom row and separator heights:

Data:    Tall bars, fat separators
Options: columns=10 rows=8 rowheight=12 sepheight=2
Encoder: codablockf

Codablock A

The Codablock A barcode symbology is a 2D stacked-linear barcode that consists of a number of stacked Code 39 symbols, each row a complete Code 39 symbol. It encodes the Code 39 character set.

Also known as: Codablock 39, Codablock Alpha.

Standards: AIM HD/13-005 Historical Document - Codablock A (ICS Codablock A symbology specification).

Data and Options

  • The data field can contain upper case letters, digits and the characters -, ., space, $, /, + and %, up to 1340 characters.
  • Each row begins and ends with a row indicator, the first row's giving the number of rows and the others the position of the row. A symbol of a single row has only the indicator at its start. Two check characters calculated over all of the data end the last row, preceded by filler spaces when the data does not fill it.
  • The columns option specifies the number of data characters in each row, from 1 to 61. The default is 8.
  • The rows option specifies the number of rows in the symbol, from 1 to 22.
  • If rows is unspecified the encoder will default to the smallest number of rows that can hold the given data.
  • The rowheight option specifies the height of the bars in each row in modules, at least 8. The default is the minimum height in the specification for the number of columns, which is about a twentieth of the width of a row and at least 8.
  • The sepheight option specifies the height of the separator bars enclosing the rows in modules, from 1 to 5. The default is 1.

Examples

Data:    THE QUICK BROWN FOX JUMPS OVER THE LAZY DOG
Options: columns=10
Encoder: codablocka

Code 11

Code 11 is a linear, discrete, non-self-checking, bidirectional, numeric barcode symbology that is primarily used for labelling telecommunication equipment.

Also known as: USD-8.

Uses:

  • Labelling telecommunications equipment.

Data and Options

  • The data consists of digits and the dash character -.
  • The includecheck option calculates the check digits.
  • For fewer than 10 data characters a single check digit is used.
  • For 10 or more data characters two check digits are used.
  • The validatecheck option takes the last digit of the data (the last two digits when the data is twelve or more characters long) to be the check digits and refuses the data if they are wrong.
  • The includecheckintext option makes the calculated check digits appear in the human readable text.

Examples

A symbol with check digits:

Data:    0123456789
Options: includecheck includetext includecheckintext
Encoder: code11

Code 16K

The Code 16K barcode symbology is a 2D stacked-linear barcode that can encode full 256 character extended-ASCII with the use of the FNC4 shift character.

Also known as: USS-16K.

Standards: ANSI/AIM BC7 - USS Code 16K, BS EN 12323.

Data and Options

  • The data field can consist of any extended ASCII data. The default interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
  • FNC4 function characters will be inserted automatically to allow the encoding of extended ASCII characters.
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • When the parsefnc option is specified, non-data function characters can be specified by escape sequences:
    • ^FNC1: FNC1
    • ^FNC2: FNC2
    • ^FNC3: FNC3
    • ^FNC@: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g. ^FNC@T... or ^FNC@99.... See FNC1 in second position. It is not available with Structured Append.
  • The sam option specifies this symbol to be part of multi-part structured data held in up to nine symbols. For example sam=25 specifies this to be the second symbol in a group of five symbols.
  • The sampos and samtotal options are an alternative to sam that give the position and the total separately, for example sampos=2 samtotal=5. They cannot be combined with sam.
  • The rows option specifies the number of rows in the symbol, between two and sixteen.
  • If rows is unspecified the encoder will default to the smallest number of rows that can hold the given data.
  • The raw option denotes that the data field is providing the input as pre-encoded codewords in ^NNN format, suitable for direct low-level encoding.
  • The rowheight option specifies the height of the bars in each row in modules, from 8 to 50. The default is 8.
  • The sepheight option specifies the height of the separator bars enclosing the rows in modules, from 1 to 5. The default is 1.

Examples

A basic symbol:

Data:    Abcd-1234567890-wxyZ
Options:
Encoder: code16k

A symbol with a fixed number of rows:

Data:    Code 16K
Options: rows=10
Encoder: code16k

A symbol with custom row and separator heights:

Data:    Tall bars, fat separators
Options: rows=8 rowheight=12 sepheight=2
Encoder: code16k

Code 25

Code 25 is a simple low density numeric barcode symbology.

Also known as: Code 25, Industrial 2 of 5, Standard 2 of 5.

Variants:

  • IATA 2 of 5, Computer Identics 2 of 5.
  • Datalogic 2 of 5.
  • Matrix 2 of 5.
  • COOP 2 of 5.

Data and Options

  • The data consists of any number of digits.
  • The includecheck option calculates the check digit.
  • The validatecheck option takes the last digit of the data to be the check digit and refuses the data if it is wrong.
  • The includecheckintext option makes the calculated check digit appear in the human readable text.
  • Deprecated: The version option determines which variant to use:
    • version=industrial (default) - Industrial 2 of 5.
    • version=iata - Deprecated: Consider IATA 2 of 5
    • version=datalogic - Deprecated: Consider Datalogic 2 of 5
    • version=matrix - Deprecated: Consider Matrix 2 of 5
    • version=coop - Deprecated: Consider COOP 2 of 5

Examples

A basic symbol:

Data:    01234567
Options:
Encoder: code2of5

Industrial 2 of 5 with a check digit, using the dedicated encoder:

Data:    01234567
Options: includetext includecheck includecheckintext
Encoder: industrial2of5

DotCode

The DotCode symbology is a 2D matrix-style barcode that can encode full 256 character extended-ASCII.

Also known as: Ribbon Code.

Uses:

  • High-speed marking on production lines, such as by inkjet.
  • Unit packets of tobacco products under EU traceability Regulation (EU) 2018/574.

Variants:

  • GS1 DotCode is a variant of DotCode that should be used when encoding data that is in GS1 Application Identifier standard format.

Standards: AIM - ISS DotCode.

Data and Options

  • The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1. When supported by the receiver, characters from other code pages can be encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value. This is useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • When the parsefnc option is specified, non-data function characters can be specified by escape sequences:
    • ^FNC1: FNC1. Recommendation: Consider GS1 DotCode for encoding GS1 AI syntax data.
    • ^FNC3: FNC3
    • ^ECI000000 to ^ECI999999: ECI indicators
    • ^FNC@: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data or of a message segment that follows FNC3, e.g. ^FNC@T... or ^FNC@99.... See FNC1 in second position.
    • ECIs are not available with FNC1 in first or second position.
  • The ratio option sets the width-to-height ratio of the symbol. The default is 1.5.
  • The columns and rows options are used to specify the size of the symbol, each from 5 to 200, with an odd sum. When these are not specified a symbol is generated that maintains the selected aspect ratio.
  • The mask option selects mask 0 to 3 instead of the best one.
  • Deprecated. The fast option is used to enable the optional high-speed symbol masking algorithm.
  • The sampos and samtotal options make the symbol one of a Structured Append sequence of 2 to 35 symbols, which a reader reassembles into a single message. Both are required:
    • sampos is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to samtotal.
    • samtotal is the number of symbols in the sequence.
    • The position and total are encoded at the end of the data, followed by FNC2.
    • Structured Append is not available with FNC3, for reader initialisation or symbol separation, nor for GS1 DotCode symbols.

Examples

A basic symbol:

Data:    This is DotCode
Options: inkspread=0.16
Encoder: dotcode

A symbol with custom aspect ratio:

Data:    Code 2.5
Options: ratio=2.5
Encoder: dotcode

Ultracode

The Ultracode symbology is a colour, 2D matrix-style barcode symbology that can encode full 256 character extended-ASCII.

Standards: AIM ISS - Ultracode.

Data and Options

  • The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • When the parsefnc option is specified, non-data function characters can be specified by escape sequences:
    • ^FNC1: FNC1
    • ^FNC3: FNC3
  • The eclevel option is used to specify the error correction level:
    • eclevel=EC1 - Low
    • eclevel=EC2 - Medium (default)
    • eclevel=EC3
    • eclevel=EC4
    • eclevel=EC5 - Highest
  • Deprecated: eclevel=EC0, error detection only, is accepted only with rev=1, the legacy revision.
  • The sampos and samtotal options make the symbol one of a Structured Append Group of 2 to 8 symbols, which a reader reassembles into a single message. Both are required:
    • sampos is the position of the symbol in the group, from 1 to samtotal.
    • samtotal is the number of symbols in the group.
    • The optional File Number of a Structured Append Group is not supported.
    • Structured Append is not available for revision 1 symbols, with FNC1 in first position, with FNC3 or with the raw option.

Examples

A symbol with increased error correction:

Data:    Nice colours!
Options: eclevel=EC3
Encoder: ultracode

IATA 2 of 5

IATA 2 of 5 is a variant of the Code 2 of 5 barcode symbology.

Also known as: Computer Identics 2 of 5.

Variants:

  • Industrial 2 of 5, Standard 2 of 5.

  • The includecheckintext option makes the calculated check digit appear in the human readable text.

Examples

A symbol with a check digit:

Data:    01234567
Options: includetext includecheck includecheckintext
Encoder: iata2of5

Matrix 2 of 5

Matrix 2 of 5 is a variant of the Code 2 of 5 barcode symbology.

Variants:

  • Industrial 2 of 5, Standard 2 of 5.
  • IATA 2 of 5, Computer Identics 2 of 5.

A symbol with a check digit:

Data:    01234567
Options: includetext includecheck includecheckintext
Encoder: matrix2of5

Datalogic 2 of 5 is a variant of the Code 2 of 5 barcode symbology.

Variants:

  • Industrial 2 of 5, Standard 2 of 5.

COOP 2 of 5

COOP 2 of 5 is a variant of the Code 2 of 5 barcode symbology.

Variants:

  • Industrial 2 of 5, Standard 2 of 5.
  • IATA 2 of 5, Computer Identics 2 of 5.

  • Matrix 2 of 5.

Data and Options

  • The data consists of any number of digits.

  • The includecheckintext option makes the calculated check digit appear in the human readable text.

A symbol with a check digit:

Data:    01234567
Options: includetext includecheck includecheckintext
Encoder: coop2of5

Code 49

The Code 49 barcode symbology is a 2D stacked-linear barcode that can encode 128 character ASCII.

Also known as: USS-49.

Standards: ANSI/AIM BC6 - USS Code 49.

Data and Options

  • The input can consist of any ASCII data.
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • When the parsefnc option is specified, non-data function characters can be specified by escape sequences:
    • ^FNC1: FNC1
    • ^FNC2: FNC2
    • ^FNC3: FNC3
    • ^FNC@: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application indicator at the start of the data, e.g. ^FNC@T.... See FNC1 in second position. Code 49 can encode an upper case letter, or a lower case letter except with append, but not two digits. It is not available with Structured Append.
  • The sam option specifies this symbol is part of multi-part structured data held in up to nine "mode 3" symbols. For example sam=25 specifies this to be the second symbol in a group of five symbols.
  • The sampos and samtotal options are an alternative to sam that give the position and the total separately, for example sampos=2 samtotal=5. They cannot be combined with sam.
  • The append option specifies that this symbol is an alphanumeric continuation symbol ("mode 1").
  • The rows option specifies the number of rows in the symbol, between 2 and 8.
  • If rows is unspecified the encoder will default to the smallest number of rows that can hold the given data.
  • The rowheight option specifies the height of the bars in each row in modules, from 8 to 50. The default is 8.
  • The sepheight option specifies the height of the separator bars enclosing the rows in modules, from 1 to 5. The default is 1.

Examples

A basic symbol:

Data:    MULTIPLE ROWS IN CODE 49
Options:
Encoder: code49

A symbol with a fixed number of rows:

Data:    CODE 49
Options: rows=8
Encoder: code49

A symbol with custom row and separator heights:

Data:    Tall bars, fat separators
Options: rows=8 rowheight=12 sepheight=2
Encoder: code49

Code One

Code One was the earliest public domain 2D matrix-style barcode. It can encode full 256 character extended-ASCII.

Also known as: Code 1, Code 1S.

Standards: AIM USS - Code One.

Data and Options

  • The data field can consist of any extended ASCII data for standard and T-type symbols. The default interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1. When supported by the receiver, characters from other code pages can be encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI).
  • Note: S-type symbols are special in that they represent a numeric value so may only contain digits.
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters, e.g. ^029 for GS, etc.
  • When the parsefnc option is specified, non-data function characters can be specified by escape sequences:
    • ^FNC1: FNC1
    • ^FNC3: FNC3
    • ^ECI000000 to ^ECI999999: ECI indicators
    • ^FNC@: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g. ^FNC@T... or ^FNC@99.... See FNC1 in second position.
    • ECIs are not available with FNC1 in first or second position.
  • The version option is used to specify the size and type of the symbol:
    • version=A to version=H - for standard format symbols (default automatic selection)
    • version=T-16, version=T-32, version=T-48 - T-type symbols
    • version=S-10, version=S-20, version=S-30 - S-type symbols
  • The sampos and samtotal options make the symbol one of a Structured Append sequence of 2 to 128 symbols, which a reader reassembles into a single message. Both are required:
    • sampos is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to samtotal.
    • samtotal is the number of symbols in the sequence. Up to 15 symbols are encoded in Group mode, and more in Extended Group mode.
    • Structured Append is not available for S-Type symbols, with FNC1 in first or second position or with reader programming (FNC3).

Examples

A standard symbol, automatically sized:

Data:    Code One
Options:
Encoder: codeone

A version C standard symbol:

Data:    Code One
Options: version=C
Encoder: codeone

A T-type symbol:

Data:    Code One
Options: version=T-32
Encoder: codeone

An S-type symbol encoding numeric data:

Data:    406990
Options: version=S-10
Encoder: codeone

Grid Matrix

The Grid Matrix symbology is a 2D matrix-style barcode symbology that can encode full 256 character extended-ASCII, with a compact encodation of Chinese characters.

Standards: AIM ISS - Grid Matrix (AIMD014), GB/T 27766.

Data and Options

  • The data field can contain any extended ASCII data. The default interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with GB 2312, in its EUC-CN form that includes ASCII. When supported by the receiver characters from other code pages can be encoded using Extended Channel Interpretation (ECI), for example ^ECI000003 for ISO/IEC 8859-1.
  • Data containing the two-byte EUC-CN form of GB 2312 characters is encoded compactly.
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • When the parsefnc option is specified, non-data function characters can be specified by escape sequences:
    • ^FNC1: FNC1
    • ^ECI000000 to ^ECI811799: ECI indicators
    • ^FNC@: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g. ^FNC@T... or ^FNC@99.... See FNC1 in second position.
    • An FNC1 before any data, or FNC1 in second position, selects FNC1 mode, in which any further FNC1 is a field separator. Without FNC1 mode an FNC1 after data cannot be encoded.
    • ECIs are not available with FNC1 in first or second position.
  • The eclevel option is used to specify the error correction level, which reserves a proportion of the codewords for error correction:
    • eclevel=1 - 10%
    • eclevel=2 - 20%
    • eclevel=3 - 30%
    • eclevel=4 - 40%
    • eclevel=5 - 50%
    • eclevel=loose - the minimum recommended level of the size of symbol: 4 for version 1, 2 for version 2 and 1 for larger symbols. This gives the greatest capacity.
    • If unspecified the level is the recommended level of the size of symbol: 5 for version 1, 4 for versions 2 and 3, and 3 for larger symbols.
    • Level 1 is not available in version 1 symbols.
  • The fixedeclevel option will prevent the error correction level from being opportunistically raised when a better fit to the current matrix is possible.
  • The version option is used to specify the size of the symbol, 1 to 13, which is 18x18 to 162x162 modules.
  • If unspecified the encoder will select the version of the symbol that is the minimum size to represent the given data at the selected error correction level.
  • The readerinit option denotes that the symbol is used for programming the barcode reader. It is not available with FNC1 in first or second position.
  • The sampos and samtotal options make the symbol one of a Structured Append sequence of 2 to 16 symbols, which a reader reassembles into a single message. Both are required:
    • sampos is the position of the symbol in the sequence, from 1 to samtotal.
    • samtotal is the number of symbols in the sequence.
    • samid is a file signature from 0 to 255, the same in every symbol of the sequence, which keeps the symbols of different sequences apart. The default is 0.
    • FNC1 in first or second position, and readerinit, are only available in the first symbol of a sequence.

Examples

A symbol with the default error correction level:

Data:    Real knowledge is to know the extent of one's ignorance.
Options:
Encoder: gridmatrix

The Chinese characters for "Welcome", given as their GB 2312 bytes:

Data:    ^187^182^211^173^185^226^193^217
Options: parse
Encoder: gridmatrix

UTF-8 text declared by ECI 26, with maximum error correction:

Data:    ^ECI000026Cr^195^168me br^195^187l^195^169e
Options: parse parsefnc eclevel=5
Encoder: gridmatrix

The first of a Structured Append sequence of two symbols that together carry the opening of Moby-Dick:

Data:    Call me Ishmael. Some years ago - never mind how long precisely -
Options: sampos=1 samtotal=2 samid=42
Encoder: gridmatrix

Datastrip 2D

The Datastrip 2D symbology is a 2D barcode symbology in the form of a strip of rows of a fixed width, read by a swipe reader, that carries a field of text or binary data in compressed form with Reed-Solomon error correction.

Standards: ANSI/AIM BC15 - Datastrip 2D.

Data and Options

  • The data field is the content of a single field of the symbol, which is text unless the fieldtype option says otherwise. It is compressed in the zlib format before being encoded.
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • The fieldtype option gives the type of the field: text (the default), jpeg, binary or jpeg2000, or a number from 0 to 255 for a reserved or proprietary type, e.g. fieldtype=16#21.
  • The fieldsubtype option gives the subtype of the field, from 0 to 255. The default is 0. For a text field 0 denotes US-ASCII, 2 UTF-16LE and 3 UTF-16BE.
  • The disposition option gives the disposition byte of the field, from 0 to 255. The default is 0. Bit 0 asks the reader not to display the field and bit 1 asks it not to transmit the field; the other bits select special processing of the field.
  • The stripid option identifies the system that created the symbol, as 12 hexadecimal digits. The default is all zeros.
  • The columns option is used to specify the width of the data area in bytes, from 4 to 19. The default is 10. The symbol is eight modules per column plus twelve modules of framing wide, within a quiet zone of two modules at each side.
  • The rows option is used to specify the number of data rows, from 31 to 3968. The symbol has four further rows of framing at each end. If unspecified the encoder will select the fewest rows that hold the data with at least a quarter of each block of bytes as error correction, which tolerates the substitution of an eighth of the block, the minimum that the specification requires.

Examples

A strip with the default width:

Data:    This is Datastrip 2D
Options:
Encoder: datastrip

A narrow strip:

Data:    Marley was dead: to begin with. There is no doubt whatever about that. The register of his burial was signed by the clergyman, the clerk, the undertaker, and the chief mourner.
Options: columns=5
Encoder: datastrip

A field of binary data:

Data:    ^000^001^002^253^254^255
Options: parse fieldtype=binary
Encoder: datastrip

MSI Plessey

MSI Plessey is a continuous, non-self-checking, arbitrary length, numeric barcode symbology.

Also known as: MSI, MSI Modified Plessey.

Uses:

  • Shelf edge labels in retail stores.

Variants:

  • Plessey (UK) is the original barcode upon which MSI Modified Plessey was based.

Data and Options

  • The data can consist of any number of digits.
  • The includecheck option calculates the check digit or check digits.
  • The includecheckintext option makes the calculated check characters appear in the human readable text.
  • The validatecheck option takes the last digits of the data to be the check digits of the checktype, as many as it adds, and refuses the data if they are wrong.
  • The checktype option is used with includecheck or validatecheck to specify the type of checksum, either:
    • checktype=mod10 (default)
    • checktype=mod1010
    • checktype=mod11
    • checktype=ncrmod11
    • checktype=mod1110
    • checktype=ncrmod1110
  • The badmod11 option allows a mod-11 checksum value of 10 to be encoded with a pair of check digits 10, with any checktype containing mod11. Normally any input whose checksum evaluates to 10 is considered invalid having no correct representation.

Examples

A symbol with a mod-10 check digit:

Data:    0123456789
Options: includecheck includetext
Encoder: msi

A symbol with mod-11 then mod-10 check digits:

Data:    0123456789
Options: includecheck checktype=mod1110 includetext includecheckintext
Encoder: msi

A symbol using the badmod11 option:

Data:    0123456785
Options: includecheck checktype=mod11 badmod11 includetext includecheckintext
Encoder: msi

Marks & Spencer

Marks & Spencer is a barcode symbology derived from EAN-8 that is used by the UK retailer Marks & Spencer for internal purposes. It differs from EAN-8 by having the centre guard bars removed and by displaying an "M" and "S" on either side of the human readable text.

Also known as: M&S Barcode.

Data and Options

  • The data field takes either seven or eight digits.
  • Seven digits are taken as the eight-digit code without its leading zero.
  • The last digit is the check digit, which is verified.
  • The includetext option should normally be supplied.

Examples

A symbol with human-readable text:

Data:    06421182
Options: includetext
Encoder: mands

Plessey

Plessey is a continuous, arbitrary length barcode symbology for encoding hexadecimal data.

Variants:

  • MSI Modified Plessey is a variant of the Plessey (UK) barcode developed by the MSI Data Corporation.
  • Anker Code is a variant of the Plessey barcode used by Anker point of sale systems.

Data and Options

  • The data can contain any of the following:
    • Digits 0-9
    • Capital letters A-F
  • Two mandatory check characters implementing a CRC check are automatically included.
  • The validatecheck option takes the last two characters of the data to be the check characters and refuses the data if they are wrong.
  • The includecheckintext option makes the calculated check characters appear in the human readable text.
  • The unidirectional option generates a unidirectional Plessey symbol.

Examples

Equivalent symbols, the latter displaying the two mandatory check characters:

Data:    01234ABCD
Options: includetext
Encoder: plessey

Data:    01234ABCD
Options: includetext includecheckintext
Encoder: plessey

A unidirectional symbol:

Data:    01234ABCD
Options: unidirectional
Encoder: plessey

Anker Code

Anker Code is a variant of the Plessey barcode symbology that was used on the labels of Anker point of sale systems before the advent of EAN.

Standards: AIM HD/13-007 Historical Document - Anker, Plessey and MSI.

Data and Options

  • The data can contain up to 28 of the following:
    • Digits 0-9
    • Capital letters A-F
  • Two mandatory check characters are automatically included. They are the complement of the CRC check characters of Plessey.
  • The symbol has the start pattern of Plessey and ends with a wide termination bar and the reverse code, which allows reading in either direction.
  • The validatecheck option takes the last two characters of the data to be the check characters and refuses the data if they are wrong.
  • The includecheckintext option makes the calculated check characters appear in the human readable text.

Examples

Data:    1234567890
Options: includetext includecheckintext
Encoder: anker

PosiCode

PosiCode is a continuous, variable length, non-self-checking, bidirectional barcode symbology that is designed for use within printing processes where it is difficult to precisely control the width of a bar.

Uses:

  • Direct part marking where bar widths are hard to control, such as laser engraving, chemical etching, dot peen or indent marking.

Standards: ITS PosiCode.

Data and Options

  • The data field can hold the following:
    • For standard symbols: Any extended ASCII data. The default interpretation of data by readers is in accordance with ISO/IEC 8859-1.
      • FNC4 function characters will be inserted automatically to allow the encoding of extended ASCII characters.
    • For limited symbols: letters A-Z, digits 0-9, symbols - and .
  • The version option is used to specify the variant of the symbol, either:
    • version=a (default)
    • version=b
    • version=limiteda
    • version=limitedb
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters, e.g. ^029 for GS, etc.
  • When the parsefnc option is specified, non-data function characters can be specified by escape sequences:
    • ^FNC1: FNC1
    • ^FNC2: FNC2
    • ^FNC3: FNC3
    • ^FNC@: FNC1 in second position, written before an AIM application indicator of one letter or two digits at the start of the data, e.g. ^FNC@T... or ^FNC@99.... See FNC1 in second position. It is not available in the limited versions.
  • The inkspread option can be used to adjust the width of the bars.

Examples

PosiCode

Equivalent ways to generate a PosiCode A symbol:

Data:    Abc123
Options: 
Encoder: posicode
Data:    Abc123
Options: version=a
Encoder: posicode

PosiCode A including a GS (ASCII 29) character:

Data:    AB^029CD
Options: parse
Encoder: posicode

PosiCode A including an FNC2 special character:

Data:    AB^FNC2CD
Options: parsefnc
Encoder: posicode

PosiCode B symbol with widened bars:

Data:    Abc123
Options: version=b inkspread=-1
Encoder: posicode

Limited PosiCode

Limited PosiCode A:

Data:    ABC-12.3
Options: version=limiteda
Encoder: posicode

Limited PosiCode B:

Data:    ABC-12.3
Options: version=limitedb
Encoder: posicode

Telepen

Telepen is an arbitrary length barcode symbology for encoding all 128 ASCII characters without the need for shift characters.

Also known as: Telepen Alpha, Telepen Full ASCII.

Uses:

  • Library books and library cards, chiefly in UK libraries.

Variants:

  • Telepen Numeric is a variant for efficient encoding of numeric data.

Standards: USS Telepen.

Data and Options

  • The data can contain any standard ASCII data, values 0-127.
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • The mandatory check digit is automatically included.
  • Deprecated: Use Telepen Numeric instead. When the numeric option is given, the data is read as either pairs of digits or 0X, 1X, etc. The singular values ^000 to ^015 and ^127 can also be encoded using the parse option.

Examples

A basic symbol:

Data:    Telepen
Options: includetext
Encoder: telepen

A symbol using the parse option to encode a carriage return:

Data:    Telepen^013
Options: parse
Encoder: telepen

Telepen Numeric

Telepen Numeric is a variant of the Telepen symbology for efficient encoding of numeric data.

Variants:

  • Telepen is the full ASCII form.

Standards: USS Telepen.

Data and Options

  • The data is provided as pairs of digits, where the second digit of a pair may be X, as in 0X, 1X, etc. The singular values ^000 to ^015 and ^127 can also be encoded using the parse option.
  • With the parse option, ^016 (DLE) switches the rest of the data to full ASCII, for example for an odd final digit or a suffix. It cannot be the first character.
  • When the parse option is specified, any instances of ^NNN in the data field are replaced with their equivalent ASCII value, useful for specifying unprintable characters.
  • The mandatory check digit is automatically included.

Examples

A symbol encoding pairs of digits:

Data:    123456
Options:
Encoder: telepennumeric

A symbol encoding data that includes X digits:

Data:    1X345X
Options:
Encoder: telepennumeric

Kodak Patch Codes

The symbol encoder generates the patch codes that Kodak document scanners recognise to separate batches and to switch scanning modes.

Uses:

  • Separator sheets that assign an image level to a document in a batch, or that switch between bi-tonal and colour scanning.

Standards: Kodak A-61599, Patch Code Information for Kodak Scanners.

Data and Options

  • The data field accepts one of the following values:
    • patch1 - Patch 1
    • patch2 - Patch 2, which assigns image level 2 to the current document
    • patch3 - Patch 3, which assigns image level 3 to the current document
    • patch4 - Patch 4, the toggle patch
    • patch6 - Patch 6
    • patcht - Patch T, the transfer patch, which assigns the predefined image level to the next document
  • The symbol is drawn at its specified size: bars and spaces 0.08 or 0.20 inches wide, 0.80 inches in all, with bars 2.5 inches long. Scanners require the bars to be parallel to the leading edge of the document and at least 0.25 inches from other printing.

Examples

Patch 2:

Data:    patch2
Options:
Encoder: symbol

The transfer patch:

Data:    patcht
Options:
Encoder: symbol

The toggle patch:

Data:    patch4
Options:
Encoder: symbol

VIN

The Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) symbol is a Code 39 barcode, without a symbol check character, carrying the 17-character number that identifies a road vehicle.

Uses:

  • Vehicle labels and documents.

Standards: ISO 3779 Road vehicles - Vehicle identification number (VIN) - Content and structure; US 49 CFR Part 565 Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) Requirements. These define the number; its Code 39 form is industry practice.

Data and Options

  • The data field is the 17-character VIN, of digits and upper case letters other than I, O and Q.
  • The check digit in the ninth position is required of every vehicle for the US market, and is verified when the World Manufacturer Identifier begins with a digit from 1 to 5, for North America. Elsewhere the ninth position may be any VIN character.
  • The options of Code 39 are available, such as hidestars to omit the asterisks from the human readable text, except for those of the symbol check character.

Examples

Data:    1ZZAB12C8DE345678
Options: includetext
Encoder: vin

LOGMARS

LOGMARS (Logistics Applications of Automated Marking and Reading Symbols) is the use of Code 39 by the US Department of Defense for marking unit packs, outer containers and documents.

Standards: MIL-STD-1189B Standard Department of Defense Bar Code Symbology.

Data and Options

  • The data field can contain the characters of Code 39: digits, upper case letters, space and -, ., $, /, +, %, up to 30 characters including any check character.
  • The human readable text omits the start and stop characters, as the standard requires.
  • The includecheck option adds the optional modulo 43 check character. The other options of Code 39 are available.
  • The X-dimension of the standard for general applications is from 0.190mm to 0.508mm. Under the physical specification options the minimum height is that of the density of the X-dimension: 6.35mm from 6.5 characters per inch, 9.53mm from 3.0, and 19.05mm below.

Examples

Data:    BOX 42 OF 100
Options: includetext
Encoder: logmars

DX Film Edge

The DX Film Edge barcode is exposed as a latent image along the edge of 135 (35mm) photographic film to identify the film for automated photofinishing, as a data track beside a clock track that synchronises its reading.

Standards: ISO 1007 Photography - 135-size film and magazine - Specifications; US Patent 4,965,628.

Data and Options

  • The data field is the DX number, optionally followed by / and the frame number:
    • The DX number is either its two parts separated by a hyphen, Part 1, the product code, from 1 to 127 and Part 2, the generation, from 0 to 15, e.g. 79-7; or the DX extract of up to four digits, e.g. 1271; or the six digits of the full DX number, e.g. 012710, whose first and last digits are not encoded.
    • The frame number is from 0 to 63, optionally followed by A for a half frame. S and X stand for frame 62, K and 00 for frame 63, and F for frame 0.
  • The rowheight option specifies the height of each track in modules. The default is 3.

Examples

Data:    79-7/22A
Options:
Encoder: dxfilmedge

Without a frame number:

Data:    1271
Options:
Encoder: dxfilmedge

GS1 Composite Symbols

GS1 Composite barcode symbologies consist of a primary component beneath a 2D component (variations of MicroPDF417 and PDF417) used to encode supplementary GS1 formatted data.

Uses:

  • Small healthcare items, such as vials and ampoules, carrying a batch and expiry date with the GTIN; consider GS1 DataMatrix, which GS1 prefers.

Variants:

  • EAN-13 Composite is a variant of EAN-13.
  • EAN-8 Composite is a variant of EAN-8.
  • UPC-A Composite is a variant of UPC-A.
  • UPC-E Composite is a variant of UPC-E.
  • GS1 DataBar Omnidirectional Composite is a variant of GS1 DataBar Omnidirectional.
  • GS1 DataBar Stacked Omnidirectional Composite is a variant of GS1 DataBar Stacked Omnidirectional.
  • GS1 DataBar Expanded Composite is a variant of GS1 DataBar Expanded.
  • GS1 DataBar Expanded Stacked Composite is a variant of GS1 DataBar Expanded Stacked.
  • GS1 DataBar Truncated Composite is a variant of GS1 DataBar Truncated.
  • GS1 DataBar Stacked Composite is a variant of GS1 DataBar Stacked.
  • GS1 DataBar Limited Composite is a variant of GS1 DataBar Limited.
  • GS1-128 Composite is a variant of GS1-128.

Data syntax: GS1 Application Identifiers.

Standards: ISO/IEC 24723, ITS EAN.UCC Composite Symbology, AIM ISS - EAN.UCC Composite Symbology, GS1 General Specifications.

Data and Options

  • The data field consists of a primary and secondary component separated by a pipe | character.
  • The data for the primary component (preceding the pipe) is entered in a format identical to the corresponding non-composite barcode symbology.
  • The data for the 2D component (following the pipe) is entered in GS1 Application Identifier standard format.
  • Note that it is not necessary to specify FNC1 characters since the encoder will insert these automatically where necessary.
  • Deprecated. The dontlint option disables GS1 Application Identifier syntax validation allowing images to be generated for input that does not comply with GS1 standards.
  • For maximum efficiency, if the data for the 2D component contains a number of application identifiers matching any of the specifications below then they should be provided in this given order:
    • (11)...(10)...
    • (17)...(10)...
    • (90){0-3 digits not starting 0}{upper alpha}...
  • The ccversion option is used to select a specific 2D component, and is normally left to the default:
    • ccversion=a - CC-A
    • ccversion=b - CC-B
    • ccversion=c - CC-C (GS1-128 Composite only)
    • If ccversion is not specified a CC-A component will be selected if the data will fit, otherwise a CC-B component will be used. In the case of GS1-128 Composite a CC-C component will be used if the data does not fit within either a CC-A or CC-B component.
  • The gs1-cc encoder draws the 2D component alone, and its cccolumns option sets the component's width in columns: 2 to 4 for CC-A and CC-B, and up to 30 for CC-C.

EAN-13 Composite

Data:    9520123456788|(99)1234-abcd
Options: includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: ean13composite

EAN-8 Composite

Data:    95200002|(21)A12345678
Options: includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: ean8composite

UPC-A Composite

Data:    012345000058|(99)1234-abcd
Options: includetext
Encoder: upcacomposite

UPC-E Composite

Data:    01234558|(15)021231
Options: includetext
Encoder: upcecomposite

GS1 DataBar Omnidirectional Composite

Data:    (01)09521234543213|(11)990102
Options: 
Encoder: databaromnicomposite

GS1 DataBar Stacked Omnidirectional Composite

Data:    (01)09521234543213|(11)990102
Options: 
Encoder: databarstackedomnicomposite

GS1 DataBar Expanded Composite

Data:    (01)09521234543213(3103)001234|(91)1A2B3C4D5E
Options: 
Encoder: databarexpandedcomposite

GS1 DataBar Expanded Stacked Composite

Data:    (01)09521234543213(10)ABCDEF|(21)12345678
Options: segments=4
Encoder: databarexpandedstackedcomposite

GS1 DataBar Truncated Composite

Data:    (01)09521234543213|(11)990102
Options: 
Encoder: databartruncatedcomposite

GS1 DataBar Stacked Composite

Data:    (01)09521234543213|(17)010200
Options: 
Encoder: databarstackedcomposite

GS1 DataBar Limited Composite

Data:    (01)09521234543213|(21)abcdefghijklmnopqrst
Options: 
Encoder: databarlimitedcomposite

GS1-128 Composite

GS1-128 Composite with a CC-A 2D component:

Data:    (01)09521234543213|(21)A1B2C3D4E5F6G7H8
Options: 
Encoder: gs1-128composite

GS1-128 Composite with a CC-C 2D component:

Data:    (00)095287654321012346|(02)09521234543213(37)24(10)1234567ABCDEFG
Options: ccversion=c
Encoder: gs1-128composite

CC-A

Isolated CC-A 2D component:

Data:    (01)09521234543213
Options: ccversion=a cccolumns=3
Encoder: gs1-cc

CC-B

Isolated CC-B 2D component:

Data:    (01)09521234543213(3103)000123
Options: ccversion=b cccolumns=4
Encoder: gs1-cc

CC-C

Isolated CC-C 2D component:

Data:    (02)09521234543213(37)24(10)1234567ABCDEFG
Options: ccversion=c cccolumns=5
Encoder: gs1-cc

Raw Symbols

DAFT

DAFT is an encoder for directly specifying the sequence of descender, ascender, full-height and tracker bars of a custom 4 state barcode symbol.

Data and Options

  • The data field contains a sequence of the characters D, A, F or T to denote the descender, ascender, full-height and tracker bars of a custom 4 state symbol.

Examples

A custom 4-state symbol:

Data:    FATDAFTDAD
Options:
Encoder: daft

Flattermarken

Flattermarken are identification marks used in book production that facilitate the proper arrangement of bound sections by a book binder.

Data and Options

  • The data field holds a sequence of digits, each a group of nine modules:
    • 1-9: a single mark at that module of the group
    • 0: the group is left blank
  • The inkspread option can be used to adjust the width of the bars.
  • If greater fidelity is required then the raw encoder should be used instead.

Examples

Marks in the first, second and fourth groups, at modules 1, 3 and 4:

Data:    1304
Options: inkspread=-1
Encoder: flattermarken

Raw

The raw encoder is used for directly specifying the space/bar succession of a custom barcode symbol.

Data and Options

  • The data field contains an alternating sequence of widths (1 to 9) for the bars and spaces of a custom symbol, starting with a bar, in modules.

Examples

A custom barcode specifying bar/space widths directly:

Data:    331132131313411122131311333213114131131221323
Options: height=0.5
Encoder: raw

Partial Symbols

EAN-2

EAN-2 is the two-digit add-on code that accompanies an EAN or UPC type barcode symbol such as an ISSN.

Also known as: Two-Digit Add-On, Two-Digit Supplement, UPC-2.

Uses:

  • The issue number of a magazine or other periodical, beside its ISSN or UPC barcode.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15420, GS1 General Specifications.

Note: The use of a two-digit add-on with EAN-8 is not defined by any symbology standard.

Deprecated. Standalone use of the EAN-2 encoder is discouraged. It is better to include an add-on by specifying the supplement's value as an extension to the data for the primary symbol. For example, 0317-8471 03 17 for a symbol representing the ISSN 0317-8471 (having sequence number 03) and with issue number 17 denoted using a two-digit add-on.

Data and Options

  • The data field must contain two digits.
  • For a periodical, the add-on usually carries the issue number, such as 01 to 12 for a monthly or 01 to 53 for a weekly, according to the PPA's barcoding guidelines.
  • The includetext option should normally be supplied.

Examples

A standalone two-digit add-on:

Data:    05
Options: includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: ean2

EAN-5

EAN-5 is the five-digit add-on code that accompanies an EAN or UPC type barcode symbol such as an ISBN or ISSN.

Also known as: Five-Digit Add-On, Five-Digit Supplement, UPC-5.

Uses:

  • The suggested retail price of a book, beside its ISBN barcode.

Standards: ISO/IEC 15420, GS1 General Specifications.

Note: The use of a five-digit add-on with EAN-8 is not defined by any symbology standard.

Deprecated. Standalone use of the EAN-5 encoder is discouraged. It is better to include an add-on by specifying the supplement's value as an extension to the data for the primary symbol. For example, 978-1-873671-00-9 54499 for a symbol representing the ISBN 978-1-873671-00-9 with suggested retail price $44.99 denoted using a five-digit add-on.

Data and Options

  • The data field must contain five digits.
  • For a book, the add-on carries the suggested retail price, according to the BISG barcoding guidelines: 5 followed by the price in US cents, such as 51995 for $19.95; 90000 when there is no suggested price; and 59999 for a price above $99.98, which is then not encoded. 00000 and 50000 are not used.
  • The includetext option should normally be supplied.

Examples

A standalone five-digit add-on:

Data:    90200
Options: includetext guardwhitespace
Encoder: ean5
